3D graphics (WebGL) are switched off in: Wotsi 3D nɔnɔmetatawo (WebGL) le web-browser sia me. Ʋu hardware acceleration le browser ƒe ɖoɖowo me eye nàgbugbɔ adze browser la gɔme be nàkpɔ 3D hall la.
A “Setu” coin with a bull on the obverse: “Setu” gaku aɖe si ŋu nyitsu le le eƒe ŋgɔgbe. Nya Setu — tɔdzisasrã si yi Lanka, le Rameswaram — dze le titinaɣeyiɣiwo me Tamil dziɖula siwo nɔ Jaffna fiaɖuƒea ƒe nuwuwu ƒe gakuwo dzi; nyitsu si le aba dzi, si nye Shiva’s Nandi, ye nye woƒe mɔ̃ si wozãna zi geɖe.
A burial urn of the kind that made Adich: Ameɖibɔ si ƒomevi na Adichanallur xɔ ŋkɔ. Wotsɔa ame kukuwo — alo woƒe ƒu siwo woƒo ƒu — dea nugo mawo tɔgbe me kple yɔdonuwo eye woɖia wo ɖe kpe gbadzɛ si le Thamirabarani tame la me. Nugoeawo nye kadodo tẽ kple Sangam hakpanyawo ƒe முதுமக்கள் தாழி .
A catalogue of the coins issued by the C: Gaku siwo Chera, Chola, kple Pandya fiawo ɖe ɖe go ƒe ŋkɔwo ƒe xexlẽdzesi, kple woƒe fia ƒe dzesi siwo nye dati, amegãxi, kple tɔmelã.
A ceramic vessel from Adichanallur. Smal: Ceramic-go aɖe si tso Adichanallur. Wotsɔa ze suewo abe esiawo ene dana ɖe ameɖibɔwo me alo wo xa, ɖewohĩ wotsɔa nuɖuɖu, tsi alo vɔsasa na ame kukuwo ɖona — si nye Gaɣeyiɣia me dzixɔse le mɔzɔzɔ si yi ŋgɔ wu ku me ƒe dzesi sue aɖe.
A chariot for a creeper, a shawl for a p: Tasiaɖam na lã si nɔa tsatsam, awudziwui na akpakpa, atikutsetse si naa agbe na hakpanyaŋlɔla: nuƒlelawo ƒe nunana xɔŋkɔwo dzena abe ɖe womewɔa dɔ o ene, eye esiae nye woƒe nya. Kodai madam nye dɔmenyonyo si bɔ ale gbegbe be nunala la mebua nunana la zazã ƒe akɔnta o — dɔmetɔtrɔ keke ta ɖe lãwo, numiemiewo kple nusɔsrɔ̃ siaa ŋu.
A Chera coin in the collection of the Na: Chera gaku aɖe si le Napier Blemanudzraɖoƒe, Thiruvananthapuram, ƒe nudzraɖoƒe. Chera gakuwo ƒe nɔnɔmee nye dati kple aŋutrɔ, si nye fiaƒomea ƒe dzesi, eye kpɔɖeŋu gbãtɔ geɖewo tso Karur, si nye Cheratɔwo ƒe titina le Amaravathitɔwo dzi.
A chieftain of the Ay line in the southe: Ay-ƒomea ƒe amegã aɖe le Podiyil (Pothigai) ƒe togbɛwo ƒe dzigbe gome. Kɔnyinyi nyanyɛ aɖe gblɔ tso eƒe awu xɔasi aɖe si wòtsɔ na mawu aɖe, si woyɔna zi geɖe be Shiva — nana be enye ɖokuitsɔtsɔna kpakple dɔmenyonyo.
A chieftain of the Malaiyaman lineage, o: Malaiyaman ƒomea me tɔ aɖe, si tso dukɔ si ƒo xlã Mullur kple Tirukkoyilur me, ɖo ŋku eƒe nunana nyui na hakpanyaŋlɔlawo kple amesiwo katã va egbɔ ta. Eƒe nɔƒe le ame adreawo dome ɖee fia be wotsɔa eƒe nunana dzidzea dziɖula ƒe bubu abe alesi wòdzidzea eƒe anyigbamama ene.
A Chola coin carrying Pandya royal insig: Cholatɔwo ƒe gaku aɖe si dzi Pandya fia ƒe dzesiwo le. Esi Cholatɔwo tsɔ Pandya-dukɔa va woƒe dziɖuɖu te la, wotsɔ Pandya tɔmelãawo da ɖe woawo ŋutɔ ƒe amegãxi xa — aʋadziɖuɖu ƒe dzesi si woƒo ɖe ga me.
A city where literature, royal patronage: Du si me agbalẽwo, fia ƒe kpekpeɖeŋunana, mawusubɔsubɔ kple dugã me agbenɔnɔ do go le abe ƒe akpe eve ene.
A coin of Kulottunga Chola bearing the t: Kulottunga Chola ƒe gaku aɖe si dzi woŋlɔ ŋkɔ ɖo be “Malai Nadu konda Chola” — Cholatɔ si xɔ togbɛnyigba, si nye Chera-nyigba. Chola-fiawo ɖea gbeƒã woƒe aʋadziɖuɖuwo le dzesideŋkɔ siwo woŋlɔ ɖe woƒe gakuwo dzi kpakple esiwo wokpa ɖe woƒe nuŋɔŋlɔwo me hã me.
A coin of Kulottunga I (1070–1120 CE), w: Kulottunga I (ƒe 1070–1120 M.Ŋ.) ƒe gaku, amesi wɔ Cholatɔwo kple Ɣedzeƒe Chalukyatɔwo ƒe fliwo ɖekae eye wòɖu Cholatɔwo ƒe dziɖuɣi diditɔ kekeake eye nu dze edzi na wo dometɔ ɖeka dzi. Eƒe gakuwo yi Chola ƒomevi siwo woɖo anyi dzi kple eƒe ŋkɔ le Nagarigbe me.
A coin of Rajaraja I. His copper coins o: Rajaraja I ƒe gaku aɖe Eƒe akɔbligaku siwo nye fia si le tsitrenu kple esiwo bɔbɔ nɔ anyi, siwo woto vɛ le eƒe dziehe Sri Lanka dzi ɖuɖu vɔ megbe la, tsa le atsiaƒua ƒe go eveawo katã dzi eye wosrɔ̃ wo ƒe alafa geɖe.
A coin of the Jaffna kingdom showing a h: Jaffna fiaɖuƒea ƒe gaku aɖe si ɖe sɔ aɖe si me tɔmelã le fia. Tamil-fia siwo nɔ Jaffna (ƒe alafa 13 lia va ɖo 17 lia) ɖe gaku ɖe go le South Indiatɔwo ƒe kɔnyinyi aɖe nu, si nye ŋkuɖodzinu na kadodo kplikplikpli si le Palk-ƒuta.
A coin of the Kongu Cheras, the Chera li: Kongu Cheras ƒe gaku aɖe, Chera ƒe dzidzime si ɖu Kongu dukɔ si le Tamil nutoa ƒe ɣetoɖoƒe gome (ƒo xlã egbegbe Coimbatore, Erode kple Karur) — nuto ma ke si me wokpɔ Romatɔwo ƒe gaku gbogbo aɖewo le.
A crowned, moustached figure in profile,: Ame aɖe si do fiakuku, si ƒe ɖa le abe lãfu ene, si do jaketi si me kpe xɔasiwo le kple aɖabɛwu siwo le sisim la, kɔ atikplɔ si ƒe nugbɔ le fu ɖe dzi. Wota mo kple asiwo le fli yibɔ nyuiwo me le anyigba si me kɔ eye woklɔ awuawo le ochre, pink kple green me — si nye fiasã me awudodo ŋuti nusɔsrɔ̃ si le abe nɔnɔmetata ene le gbedoxɔ me nutata aɖe me.
A detail of the painted ceiling of the J: Jaintɔwo ƒe agado ƒe gbedoxɔ si le Sittanavasal ƒe dzisasrã si wota la ƒe akpa aɖe: lotus pink siwo ʋu le pad damawo dome, lã aɖe si le tsia me tom kple nɔnɔmetata aɖe si le seƒoƒowo ƒom ƒu. Woxlẽa ta la zi geɖe be enye samavasarana, si nye dziƒo takpekpe si me Jaintɔ Tirthankara aɖe ɖea gbeƒã le, ƒe lotus-tɔʋu, eye nuteƒewɔlawo ƒoa seƒoƒowo nu ƒu be yewoatsɔ asa vɔe.
A funerary vessel from the burial cairns: Ameɖiʋu aɖe si woɖe tso Nilgiri togbɛwo ƒe ameɖibɔwo me, eye wotsɔ nɔnɔmetata siwo wowɔ abe kpɔɖeŋu ene ɖo eƒe nutsyɔnu dzi. Ƒe alafa wuiadelia me Nilgiri-towo kukulawo ke ɖe nutsyɔnu mawo tɔgbe geɖe siwo dzi wotsɔ amewo, lãwo kple sɔdolawo ɖo la ŋu — nukpɔkpɔ suesuesue siwo wotsɔ anyi wɔ siwo ate ŋu aɖe ame kukuwo ƒe agbenɔnɔ kple woƒe nɔnɔme afia.
A garland of about a hundred and fifty a: Seƒoƒotsihe si ƒe kpukpui siwo ade alafa blaatɔ̃ akam siwo Kanimethaviyar ŋlɔ, siwo ade blaetɔ̃ na anyigba ƒe nɔnɔme atɔ̃awo dometɔ ɖesiaɖe.
A gold coin of Rajaraja I (985–1014 CE),: Rajaraja I (ƒe 985–1014 M.Ŋ.), si tu gbedoxɔ gã si le Thanjavur la ƒe sikagaku. Eɖe Cholatɔwo ƒe fia ƒe dzesi si wonya nyuie la fia: amegãxi si bɔbɔ nɔ anyi si ŋu Pandya tɔmelã eve le axadzi, le dziɖulanyenye ƒe ɣeɖuƒe aɖe te, eye fia la ƒe ŋkɔ le Nagarigbe me — Cholatɔwo gblɔna be yewoɖua dzigbe dzi.
A gold half-kahavanu of Virarajendra Cho: Virarajendra Chola (ƒe 1063–1070 M.Ŋ.) ƒe sika kahavanu afã. Kahavanu (si tso kahapana me) nye Sri Lanka ƒe sika, eye Cholatɔwo ƒe sika si woƒo ɖe dzidzenu sia nu la ɖea ɣeyiɣi si me Cholatɔwo ɖu ƒukpoa dzi fiana.
A guide poem of the Ten Idylls by Kadiya: Idylls Ewoawo ƒe mɔfiamehakpanya aɖe si Kadiyalur Uruthirankannanar ŋlɔ. Wofiaa mɔ bard aɖe si si yazh gã la le yi Thondaiman Ilanthiraiyan si tso Kanchi gbɔ; le mɔa dzi la, hakpanya la ɖe kɔƒewo, melidzeƒewo, kple amewo ƒe nukpɔkpɔ siwo me kɔ.
A guide poem of the Ten Idylls by Mudath: Idylls Ewoawo ƒe mɔfiame hakpanya aɖe si Mudathama Kanniyar ŋlɔ. Bard (porunar) si ƒoa kpẽ si woɖo eteƒe na geɖe la fiaa mɔ ehati haƒola aɖe yia Chola-fia dɔmenyotɔ Karikal Valavan gbɔ.
A guide poem of the Ten Idylls by Nallur: Idylls Ewoawo ƒe mɔfiame hakpanya aɖe si Nallur Nathathanar ŋlɔ. Saŋkuƒola aɖe si ƒoa yazh (saŋku) sue la kplɔa bubu yia amegã Nalliyakkodan gbɔ, eye wòƒoa nu tso haƒola dahewo ƒe nɔnɔme sesẽwo kple vividoɖeameŋu si ame aɖe si tsɔa saŋku ɖona la ŋu.
A guide poem of the Ten Idylls by Perunk: Idylls Ewoawo ƒe mɔfiame hakpanya aɖe si Perunkausikanar ŋlɔ. Wofiaa mɔ fefewɔla siwo le tsaglãla tsam (koothar) yia amegã Nannan gbɔ; woɖua azã na hakpanya la le esi wòlé towo ƒe gbeɖiɖi gbogboawo ɖe mɔ̃ dzi ta.
A JOURNEY THROUGH: MƆZƆZƆ SI TO AME ƑE ƲUƲU ME
A large storage jar associated with Adic: Nudzraɖoƒe gã aɖe si do ƒome kple Adichanallur. Nuku, tsi kple nuɖuɖu bubuwo nɔa ze siwo me nu geɖe le me; le ameɖiƒewo la, nugo siwo lolo alea ate ŋu anye nugoewo hã. Nya “dolio” ɖo ŋku dolium, si nye Roma-xexeame ƒe nudzraɖoƒe gã la dzi.
A large, round-bellied funerary urn from: Ameɖibɔ gã aɖe si ƒe ƒodo le goglo tso Adichanallur. Nugoe siwo le abe esia ene ate ŋu anɔ te sesĩe wu ɖevi, eye wo wɔwɔ bia aɖaŋu geɖe: Sangam hakpanyaŋlɔlawo ƒo nu na zemela si wɔa nugoewo abe கலம்செய் கோவே — “Oo fia le zemelawo dome”.
A lead coin from Andipatti bearing a leg: Gaku si wotsɔ lãgbalẽ wɔe si tso Andipatti si dzi xotutu aɖe le le Tamil-Brahmigbe me. Tsɔ kpe ɖe fia etɔ̃ siwo woɖo fiakukue ŋu la, nutoa me amegã siwo nɔ anyi le Sangam ƒe ɣeyiɣia me ɖea gaku siwo wotsɔ lifi kple akɔbli wɔe, eye Tamil-Brahmitɔwo ƒe xotutu siwo ku ɖe wo ŋu kpena ɖe ame ŋu be wotsɔ ŋkɔ na dziɖula siawo.
A line drawing of the vimana and a pilla: Vimana kple Brihadisvara Gbedoxɔa ƒe akpata si ŋu sɔtiwo le ƒe nɔnɔmetata.
A love poem of the Ten Idylls by Kapilar: Lɔlɔ̃hakpanya aɖe si ku ɖe Idylls Ewoawo ŋu si Kapilar ŋlɔ, si wowɔ le to (kurinji) ƒe nɔnɔme me. Kɔnyinyi gblɔ be woŋlɔe be woatsɔ afia dziehefia aɖe Tamiltɔwo ƒe lɔlɔ̃hakpanyawo ƒe atsyɔ̃; exɔ ŋkɔ na seƒoƒo blaasieke vɔ enyi.
A modern artist’s imagining of a busy ha: Egbegbe nutala aɖe ƒe meliwo, asiwo kple xɔ kɔkɔwo ƒe melidzeƒe si vovo mele o ƒe susu me, le nuŋlɔɖi siwo le Silappathikaram kple Pattinappalai megbe. Menye alesi dua nɔ ŋutɔŋutɔ ƒe kpeɖodzie wònye o.
A modern sketch imagining ships and buil: Egbegbe nɔnɔmetata aɖe si me woɖe meliwo kple xɔ siwo le blema melidzeƒea le susu me. Abe Puhar ƒe gbugbɔgatu ɖesiaɖe ene la, eɖea agbalẽwo me nuŋlɔɖiwo gɔme; womenya melidzeƒea ƒe ɖoɖo bliboa o.
A name linked with Nedunalvadai and Tiru: Ŋkɔ si do ƒome kple Nedunalvadai kple Tirumurukarruppatai le Idylls Ewoawo me — togbɔ be ate ŋu anye hakpanyaŋlɔla siwo wu ɖeka tɔ le ɣeyiɣi vovovowo me hã. Xotutu siwo wova do emegbe gblɔ eƒe gbegbe be yematsɔ yeƒe ʋɔnudɔdrɔ̃ le hakpanya aɖe ŋu na Shiva gɔ̃ hã le Pandya fiasã me o ŋu: enye nunya ƒe dzideƒo ƒe dzesi, ke menye ŋutinya me nudzɔdzɔ o.
A Note on the Evidence: Nyatakaka aɖe si Ku Ðe Kpeɖodziawo Ŋu
A palm-leaf manuscript from the museum’s: Asinuŋɔŋlɔgbalẽ si wotsɔ deti ƒe aŋgba wɔ tso blemanudzraɖoƒea ƒe nudzraɖoƒe.
A Pandya coin of the “massa” type. Massa: Pandya gaku si nye “massa” ƒomevi. Massa nye ŋkɔ si wotsɔ na titinaɣeyiɣiwo me akɔbli gaku siwo ɖe nɔnɔmetata si le tsitrenu fia le axa ɖeka eye nɔnɔmetata si bɔbɔ nɔ anyi le akpa kemɛ — nɔnɔmetata si Cholatɔwo kaka eye Pandyatɔwo kple Sri Lanka fiawo yi edzi.
A Pandya coin showing a standing king wi: Pandya gaku aɖe si ɖe fia aɖe si le tsitrenu si ŋu tɔmelã ƒe dzesi le fia. Dziɖula si le tsitrenu ƒe nɔnɔmetata, si Cholatɔwo ƒe akɔbligakuwo na wonya nyuie la, va zu Pandyatɔwo esime woƒe ŋusẽ gafɔ ɖe te le ƒe alafa 13 lia me.
A Pandya coin with the twin fish and a b: Pandya gaku aɖe si me tɔmelã veviwo kple nyitsu le. Tɔmelã eve eve va zu Pandya ƒe dzesi si nɔa anyi ɖaa, si wokpa ɖe hakpanyaawo ƒe Madurai aflagawo dzi eye woƒoe ɖe gakuwo dzi ƒe akpe ɖeka kple edzivɔ.
A pillared hall today: Akpata si ŋu sɔtiwo le egbea
A pipeline of terracotta rings, set one: Anyigbaʋuʋu ƒe asigɛwo ƒe pɔmpi aɖe, si woɖo ɖe wo nɔewo dzi le xɔ ene me, si woɖe ɖe go le Korkai tomenukukua me. Tɔdzisasrã siwo wotsɔ anyi wɔe kple vudo siwo wotsɔa asigɛ wɔe abe esia ene tsɔa tsi heɖea tsi le Tamil-dukɔ gbãtɔ si nye ŋutinya me duwo me — si nye melidzeƒe si amewo sɔa gbɔ ɖo ƒe gbesiagbe mɔ̃ɖaŋununya ƒe akpa aɖe.
A poem of the Ten Idylls by Kadiyalur Ur: Kadiyalur Uruthirankannanar ƒe Idylls Ewoawo ƒe hakpanya, si kafu Chola-fia Karikal Valavan kple eƒe melidzeƒedu si me ʋuʋu le si nye Kaveripoompattinam (Puhar), kple eƒe meliwo, asiwo, kple azãɖuɖuwo.
A poem of the Ten Idylls by Nakkeerar. D: Idylls Ewoawo ƒe hakpanya aɖe si Nakkeerar ŋlɔ. Le vuvɔŋɔli ƒe dzieheya si fa miamiamia le ɣeyiɣi didi aɖe me la, fianyɔnu aɖe dzroa srɔ̃a vevie esime fia la le eƒe asrafo siwo xɔ abi la dzi kpɔm le aʋasaɖa aɖe me.
A portrait coin of the Chera king Kuttuv: Chera-fia Kuttuvan Kotai ƒe nɔnɔmetata gaku aɖe, si tsɔ ŋkɔ nɛ le Tamil-Brahmigbe me. Le Makkotai gakuawo gome la, klosalo tata siawo siwo mebɔ o — siwo ɖewohĩ Romatɔwo ƒe nɔnɔmetata gaku siwo va to asitsatsa me ʋã wo — le Indiatɔwo ƒe gaku gbãtɔ siwo wotsɔ ɖe dziɖula ƒe mo fia la dome.
A potsherd inscribed in Tamil-Brahmi, fo: Ze kakɛ aɖe si woŋlɔ ɖe Tamil-Brahmigbe me, si wokpɔ le Tissamaharama le Sri Lanka ƒe dzigbe eye woŋlɔe le ƒe alafa 2 lia D.M.Ŋ. Nuŋɔŋlɔ ɖe Tamilgbe me le ze siwo le didiƒe ʋĩ tso Tamil-nyigbagã gbɔ ŋu ɖe Tamil-asitsala siwo nɔ dɔ wɔm le atsiaƒua ƒe go kemɛ dzi le ŋutinya me ɣeyiɣia ƒe gɔmedzedze fia.
A rare book from the first decades of Ta: Agbalẽ si mebɔ o tso Tamilgbe me agbalẽtata ƒe ƒe bla nane gbãtɔwo me, esime wonɔ nuŋɔŋlɔ xoxo siwo wodzra ɖo ɖe deti ƒe aŋgbawo dzi la ɖom ɖe mɔ̃ dzi zi gbãtɔ.
A rare volume digitised from CICT’s arch: Babla si mebɔ o si wotsɔ de dijitaal dzi tso CICT ƒe nudzraɖoƒe eye wodzrae ɖo hena nusɔsrɔ̃. Blemanudzraɖoƒea ƒe nudzraɖoƒedzikpɔlawo atsɔ agbalẽdzraɖoƒea ŋuti nyatakaka bliboa akpe ɖe eŋu.
Etsɔ si me Kesinɔnuwo Le Wu.
A Sangam-age Chola coin with a tiger and: Cholatɔwo ƒe gaku si nɔ anyi le Sangam ƒe ɣeyiɣia me si me amegãxi kple sɔ le. Cholatɔwo ƒe gaku gbãtɔwo, siwo ƒe akpa gãtɔ nye akɔbli, ƒe titina le amegãxi la ŋu — dzesi ma ke si fiaɖuƒea ƒe Cholatɔwo atsɔ le ƒe akpe ɖeka megbe. Uraiyur kple Kaveripoompattinam ye nye woƒe teƒe gãwo.
A Sangam-age Pandya coin, typically a sm: Pandya gaku si nɔ anyi le Sangam ƒe ɣeyiɣia me, si zi geɖe la, akɔbli sue aɖe si le dzogoe ene me si dzi sɔ le axa ɖeka eye tɔmelã si wowɔ ɖe atsyã nu le axa kemɛ. Gaku mawo nɔa tsatsam le Madurai, si nye Pandya ƒe fiadu si woɖua azã le Maduraikkanchi, kple eƒe nutowo me.
A scholarly study of government, adminis: Agbalẽnyalagãwo ƒe numekuku tso dziɖuɖu, dɔdzikpɔkpɔ, kple hadomegbenɔnɔ ŋu le Tamil-dukɔ si nɔ anyi le Sangam ƒe ɣeyiɣia me.
A second coin of the Kongu Cheras. Compa: Kongu Cheras ƒe gaku evelia. Tsɔ evea sɔ kple wo nɔewo: gaku siwo wotsɔ asi ƒo la toa vovo le woƒe ƒoƒo, woƒe vuvu kple wo ɖeɖe me, eye vovototo mawo kpena ɖe gaŋutinunyalawo ŋu be woakpɔ nyawo gbɔ ahakpɔ ɣeyiɣi didi si gakuwo nɔ tsatsam.
A second image of the four-armed, seated: Ganesha si si alɔ ene le, si bɔbɔ nɔ anyi la ƒe nɔnɔmetata evelia. Tsɔ eƒe lolome, atsyɔ̃ɖonuwo kple atikutsetsea ƒe tɔtrɔ sɔ kple gbãtɔa: le Silpa Sastras ƒe agbalẽ si wozãna ɖekae me la, nɔnɔmetatawɔla kple dɔwɔƒe ɖesiaɖe gblẽ eya ŋutɔ ƒe asikaka ŋu ɖi.
A selection drawn from the Thirukkural,: Tiatia aɖe si woɖe tso Thirukkural me, si ƒo nya eve siwo dzi woaɖo ŋkui nu ƒu na nuxlẽlawo.
A separate photographing of the opening: Babla 579 D, si nye Maduraikkanchi, ƒe aŋgba siwo ʋuna ƒe fotoɖeɖe ɖe vovo.
Shaiva ame kɔkɔe aɖe, asiwo ƒo ƒu le tadedeagu me. Chola-fiawo de bubu Nayanmartɔ blaade vɔ etɔ̃ ŋu, amesiwo ƒe agbenɔnɔ Sekkizhar gblɔ le Periya Puranam me, eye woɖo woƒe akɔbli legbawo ɖe gbedoxɔwo me hetsɔ wo le azãɖuɖu ƒe mɔzɔzɔwo me.
A sherd illustrated in Vimala Begley’s 1: Nu kakɛ aɖe si ƒe kpɔɖeŋu le Vimala Begley ƒe numekuku si wòwɔ le ƒe 1983 me tso Arikamedu ƒe ɣeyiɣikɔntabubu ŋu. Esi Begley gbugbɔ lé ŋku ɖe ƒuƒoƒo siwo woɖe ŋu la, eʋli nya be amewo ƒe nɔƒea dze egɔme le ƒe alafa etɔ̃lia D.M.Ŋ. Eƒe ɣletiŋkekewo gakpɔtɔ nye agbalẽnyalagãwo ƒe gɔmeɖeɖe.
A sherd of an urn found in 2004, decorat: Nugoe ƒe kakɛ aɖe si ŋu woke ɖo le ƒe 2004 me, si wotsɔ nɔnɔmetata si wotsɔ lãfu wɔe ɖo atsyɔ̃ na kple nyɔnu ƒe nɔnɔmetata si le tsitrenu le nɔnɔmetata siwo woxlẽna zi geɖe be bli ƒe aŋgbawo, gbetedzi, crane kple atiglinyi dome. Agbalẽnyalagãwo kpɔ dadaa mawunɔ gbãtɔ aɖe le eŋu — abe alesi sinima la gblɔe ene la, ɖewo nye Kotravai, si nye Sangam hakpanyawo ƒe aʋawɔmawunɔ la ƒe ŋgɔdola. Enye kpɔɖeŋunɔnɔmetata siwo mebɔ o siwo le Gaɣeyiɣiwo me Tamil Nadu la dometɔ ɖeka.
A short illustrated guide for visitors:: Mɔfiame kpui aɖe si me nɔnɔmetatawo le na amedzrowo: nusiwo Sangam hakpanyawo nye, alesi woƒo wo nu ƒu ɖe hatsotsowo me, kple alesi akam kple puram hakpanyawo kple anyigba ƒe nɔnɔme atɔ̃awo wɔa dɔe.
A silver kasu of Rajendra Chola combinin: Rajendra Chola ƒe klosalo kasu si tsɔ fia ƒe dzesiwo tsaka — Chola amegãxi kple Pandya tɔmelã kple Chera dati. Rajendra I (ƒe 1014–1044 M.Ŋ.) tsɔ Cholatɔwo ƒe ŋusẽ yi Ganges eye wòtso atsiaƒua yi Anyieheɣedzeƒe Asia, eye eƒe gakuwo ɖe gbeƒãe be yeɖu Tamiltɔwo ƒe fiakuku etɔ̃awo katã dzi.
A silver kasu of the “Uttama” type, attr: Klosalo kasu si nye “Uttama” ƒomevi, si wogblɔ le afisia be Rajendra I. Ƒomea xɔ ŋkɔ tso Uttama Chola ƒe gakuwo me, amesi ƒe nɔnɔme — amegãxi, tɔmelã kple dati le ɣe ƒe keklẽ te — ɖo kpɔɖeŋu na Chola klosalo emegbe.
A simplified sequence of how cloth is ma: Alesi wowɔa avɔe ƒe ɖoɖo si le bɔbɔe. Eɖe alesi wowɔa dɔa le goawo katã me me; menye kpeɖodzi be blema Tamiltɔwo ƒe dɔwɔƒe ɖesiaɖe zɔ ɖe afɔɖeɖe siawo tututu dzi le ɖoɖo sia nu o — dɔwɔnuwo, kple ɖoɖo si nu wodea amae kple avɔlɔlɔ̃e, ate ŋu ato vovo.
A small pottery cup from the Adichanallu: Zemela ƒe kplu sue aɖe si woɖe tso Adichanallur ƒe ameɖiƒewo. Kpluwo, agbawo kple nutsyɔnuwo nɔ yɔdo me nu siwo bɔ wu dome, eye woƒe nɔnɔme si me woɖɔa ŋu ɖo, si sɔ pɛpɛpɛ la ɖea zemela siwo wɔa dɔ le tasiaɖamfɔa dzi ƒe akpe etɔ̃ kloe enye sia la fia.
A summit of Chola architecture, art and: Cholatɔwo ƒe xɔtuɖaŋu, aɖaŋudɔwo kple dɔdzikpɔkpɔ ƒe takpekpe aɖe; UNESCO ƒe Chola Gbedoxɔ Gã Gbagbewo ƒe akpa aɖe.

A village on the Noyyal in Erode distric: Kɔƒe aɖe si le Noyyal tɔsisi dzi le Erode nutoa me, si woɖe be wòanye dzonuwɔƒe, kpe xɔasiwo wɔwɔ kple gayibɔ kple gakpo wɔwɔ ƒe teƒe.

A volume connected with the Madurai Tami: Babla si do ƒome kple Madurai Tamil Sangam, agbalẽsɔsrɔ̃suku si Pandithurai Thevar ɖo le Madurai le ƒe 1901 me eye woyɔnɛ zi geɖe be “Tamil Sangam Enelia”.
A volume from the shrine’s collection of: Babla aɖe si tso Thirukkural gɔmeɖeɖe siwo woƒo ƒu le gbedoxɔa me. Kural ƒe gbedasi si ku ɖe nyuiwɔwɔ ŋu ɖo nuxlẽlawo gbɔ le India kple xexeame ƒe gbegbɔgblɔ geɖe me.
A volume on the poetry of Kambar, the gr: Babla aɖe si ƒo nu tso Kambar, Kamba Ramayanam (Ramavataram) ƒe hakpanyaŋlɔla gã, amesi ƒe Tamilgbe bibi na wòxɔ ŋkɔ “Kavichakravarthi”, hakpanyaŋlɔlawo ƒe fiagã, ƒe hakpanyawo ŋu.
A vyala or yali, the horned, lion-like g: Vyala alo yali, si nye lã si le South India gbedoxɔwo dzi dzɔla si ƒe dzo le abe dzata ene. Pallavatɔwo tsɔe de asi ete, eye woɖo sɔtiwo ɖe dzatawo kple yaliwo nyinyi ŋu le Mamallapuram kple Kanchipuram; emegbe xɔtulawo tsɔe yi gbedoxɔa ƒe akpata gãwo me.
A wall painting of Gajalakshmi from the: Gajalakshmi ƒe glitata aɖe si woɖe tso Gbedoxɔ Gã la me: mawunɔa bɔbɔ nɔ lotus-fiazikpui dzi afɔ siwo wotso ɖe wo nɔewo ŋu esime sɔ eve siwo ƒe amadede nye aŋutiɖiɖi geɖe le zewo kple lotus-tiwo kɔm ɖe eƒe ta dzi. Vɔvɔli siwo wota kpekpewo le etame kple aŋgba dama siwo le ƒoƒom le ete la ɖe alesi Nayak-ɣeyiɣia me glitatawo ƒe atsyɔ̃ɖoɖo ƒe dzidzedzekpɔkpɔ le la fia.
A workshop of Pallava art and early Tami: Pallavatɔwo ƒe aɖaŋudɔwo kple Tamiltɔwo ƒe gbedoxɔ gbãtɔwo ƒe xɔtuɖaŋu ƒe dɔwɔƒe; UNESCO ƒe Xexeame ƒe Domenyinu Teƒe aɖe.
A yogini, one of a circle of powerful go: Yogini, mawunɔ sẽŋuwo ƒe ƒuƒoƒo aɖe si wosubɔna le tantric kɔnyinyiwo me la dometɔ ɖeka. Wotsɔ kpe yogini siwo bɔbɔ nɔ anyi ƒe ƒuƒoƒo ɖedzesi aɖe do ƒome kple Kanchipuram nutoa me le Cholatɔwo ƒe ɣeyiɣia me; kpɔɖeŋuwo le blemanudzraɖoƒewo le xexeame godoo fifia.
About four hundred short akam poems of f: Akam hakpanya kpui siwo ade alafa ene siwo me fli ene va ɖo enyi le, siwo le Sangam lɔlɔ̃ hakpanyawo ƒe kpukpui siwo woyɔ wu dome.

Across the Kaveri, east of Tiruchirappal: Le Kaveri-tɔsisia ƒe go kemɛ dzi, le Tiruchirappalli ƒe ɣedzeƒe gome la, Kallanai — “kpe ƒe tɔdzisasrã” — le tsitre ɖe tsidzikpɔkpɔdɔ xoxotɔ kekeake siwo le xexeame siwo wogale zazãm la dome. Tamiltɔwo ƒe kɔnyinyi gblɔ be Karikal Chozhan, Chola-fia gbãtɔ si woɖuna le Pattinappalai, gbɔe wòtso, eye wogblɔ be ƒe alafa evelia M.Ŋ. Esi tsidzadza vuvu ta la, Kaveri-tɔsisia kɔ ɖe eƒe tɔʋua me mɔxenu aɖeke manɔmee, eye wògbã eƒe gowo eye wògblẽ agblewo dome; Menye Karikalan ƒe ŋuɖoɖoe nye be wòatɔ te tɔsisia o, ke boŋ be wòabɔbɔe ahamae. Cholatɔwo ƒe hakpanya siwo wova ŋlɔ emegbe, kple fiaƒome siwo gblɔ be yewotsoe ƒe nuŋɔŋlɔwo kafui be eyae nye fia si kɔ Kaveri-tɔsisia ƒe gowo ɖe dzi.

Adichanallur did not stand alone. Along: Adichanallur metsi tre ɖe eɖokui ŋu o. Sivakalai kple teƒe gbãtɔ bubuwo le Thamirabarani-tɔsisia to, eye tɔsisia tsɔa amewo kple adzɔnuwo yia Mannar-ƒuta, afisi Korkai tsi le va zu Pandya melidzeƒe si me dzonu kple chank le. Ga, akɔbli kple sika si woatsɔ awɔ dɔe, blinyigba nyui aɖe, kple tɔsisimɔ si yi ƒuta la nɔ balia me. Wokpɔa nugoe siwo me woɖia kɔnyinyi ma ke le le Gulf-ƒua ƒe go kemɛ dzi le Sri Lanka, eye kpe siwo le didiƒe ƒe akɔbliwo ɖo balia me — si nye dzesi gbãtɔ siwo ɖee fia be woɖɔli wo nɔewo si ana Tamil ƒuta nanye India-ƒua ƒe asitsatsa ƒe teƒe vevi aɖe le ƒe alafa ʋɛ aɖewo me. Still kple film siwo woɖe tso tomenuawo me le nugoe siwo le ete la me.

Agriculture remains an important part of: Agbledede gakpɔtɔ nye Tamil Nadu ƒe ganyawo kple kɔƒenutowo me agbenɔnɔ ƒe akpa vevi aɖe. Agblemenuku veviwo dometɔ aɖewoe nye bli, sukli, kotoklobo, anyigba, ƒaƒã, kple aŋanyi, eye woƒe agbledede ƒe ɖoɖowo toa vovo le anyigba, tsidzadza, tsidede agble, kple asiwo ƒe didi nu. Egbegbe agbledelawo zãa blema sidzedze kple egbegbe mɔ̃ɖaŋununya ƒokpli, siwo dometɔ aɖewoe nye trakt, mɔ̃ siwo wotsɔ ŋea nu, nuku siwo nyo wu, tsidede agble ƒe pɔmpiwo, kple anyigbadzikpɔkpɔ ƒe mɔnuwo. Tsidede tsi si toa tsi me kple mɔnu bubu siwo zãa tsi nyuie ate ŋu akpe ɖe ame ŋu woakpɔ tsi siwo mebɔ o dzi le agbledede ƒe ɖoɖo siwo sɔ me. Agbledelawo doa go kuxiwo abe tsidzadza si medzɔna edziedzi o, kuɖiɖi, nusiwo wozãna ƒe asi si le dzidzim ɖe edzi, dɔwɔlawo ƒe veve, kple asitsaƒewo ƒe asiwo ƒe tɔtrɔ hã. Eyata Tamil Nadu ƒe agbledede ƒe domenyinu tsi tre ɖi na ŋutinya didi aɖe si ku ɖe tɔtrɔ ɖe nutoa me ƒe nutome ƒe nɔnɔmewo ŋu kple dɔwɔƒe si le tɔtrɔm si wɔa nu ɖe ​​egbegbe ganyawo kple yame ƒe nɔnɔme ƒe nyaƒoɖeamenuwo ŋu siaa.
Agriculture was an important source of f: Agbledede nye nuɖuɖu, agbenɔnɔ, kple ganyawo ƒe dzɔtsoƒe vevi aɖe le blema Tamiltɔwo ƒe hadomegbenɔnɔ me. Sangam-gbalẽwo, siwo zi geɖe do ƒome kple ɣeyiɣi si nɔ anyi le ƒe 300 D.M.Ŋ.–300 M.Ŋ. Tamil hakpanyaŋlɔlawo tsɔ anyigba ƒe nɔnɔme vovovowo do ƒome kple agbenɔnɔ ƒe mɔnu vovovowo. Marutham-nyigba la tsi tre ɖi na agbledenyigba nyuiwo, afisi bligbledede kple agbledede bubuwo ɖe dzesi le. Agbledelawo tiaa nukuwo le anyigba ƒe nɔnɔme, tsidzadza, kple tsi si le wo si nu. Bli, aŋanyi, sukli, nuku, kotoklobo, kple sesame le nuku siwo ŋu woƒo nu tsoe le blema Tamiltɔwo ƒe agbledede ŋuti numekukuwo me la dome. Agbledede nɔ te ɖe amegbetɔ ƒe dɔwɔwɔ, lãwo ƒe ŋusẽ, kple nutoa me ƒe nɔnɔmewo ŋuti sidzedze dzi. Agbalẽ me kpeɖodziwo naa gɔmesese veviwo le agbledede ƒe agbenɔnɔ ŋu, togbɔ be ele be woaɖe wo gɔme kpe ɖe blematomenukulawo kple ŋutinya me numekukuwo ŋu hã.

All 1,330 couplets in 133 chapters — eac: Nya eve 1,330 siwo katã le ta 133 me — fli kpui eve koe wo dometɔ ɖesiaɖe le, eye aɖaŋuɖoɖowo gakpɔtɔ yɔ fũu na agbe egbea.
Also called Perumpekan. Seeing a peacock: Wogayɔnae be Perumpekan. Esi wòkpɔ akpakpa le vuvɔ me la, exatsae ɖe eya ŋutɔ ƒe awu ʋlaya xɔasi me — kodai madam ƒe nuwɔna, dɔmenyonyo si bɔ ale gbegbe be nunala la medaa nunana la o. Eƒe ŋkɔxɔxɔ nɔ te ɖe dɔmetɔtrɔ dzi tsɔ wu be wòaɖu dzi.

An animated reconstruction of the ancien: Blema mɔnu la gbugbɔgatu si me agbe le, tso nuŋlɔɖi si ku ɖe Kallanai ŋu si Central Institute of Classical Tamil wɔ me. Dɔwɔlawo kple sɔwo ƒe ƒuƒoƒowo he kpe gãwo yi tɔsisia me hetsɔ wo ƒu gbe ɖe tɔsisia to. Esi ƒutsotsoeawo nɔ ke si le wo te la ƒom ɖa la, wonyrɔ, eye kpe bubuwo ƒo ƒu ɖe wo dzi vaseɖe esime kpeawo va nɔ anyigba sesẽ dzi. Emegbe anyikpe kple tsiɖɔɖɔa ƒe tsikpewo yɔ doawo me, eye wobla kpeawo wozu dzɔdzɔmemɔxenu si me tsi mate ŋu age ɖo o.
An archaeologist cleans the shoulder of: Tomenukula aɖe dzraa nugoe gã aɖe ƒe abɔta le ameɖiƒea ƒe anyigba dzĩ la me. Tomenukulawo le ƒe 2004 me ke ɖe nugoe siwo kɔkɔ abe meta ɖeka kloe ene, siwo lolo ale gbegbe be woate ŋu axɔ ame kukuwo ƒe kukuawo. Nugo siwo lolo alea bia aɖaŋu ŋutɔŋutɔ: Sangam hakpanyaŋlɔla aɖe yɔa nugoewɔla be கலம்செய் கோவே, “Oo fia le zemela dome”.
An early engraved view of a great pillar: Fiasãa ƒe akpata gã aɖe si ŋu sɔtiwo le ƒe nɔnɔmetata si wokpa gbã. Womeŋlɔ nutala la kple ŋkeke si dzi woŋlɔe ɖe nɔnɔmetata la ŋu o.
An early engraving of a long pillared ha: Akpa didi aɖe si ŋu sɔtiwo le si ŋu wokpa sɔtiwo le, si ƒomevi wotu ƒo xlã Madurai ƒe gbedoxɔ gã la, ƒe nɔnɔmetata gbãtɔ. Womeŋlɔ nutala la kple ŋkeke si dzi woŋlɔe ɖe nɔnɔmetata la ŋu o.
An early painted view of the great templ: Gbedoxɔ gã la kple eƒe vimana siwo le dzi yim le gbadzaƒea ƒe nɔnɔmetata si wota le gɔmedzedzea me. Womeŋlɔ nutala la kple ŋkeke si dzi woŋlɔe ɖe nɔnɔmetata la ŋu o.
An early painted view of the Shore Templ: Shore Gbedoxɔ si le tsitre ɖe eƒe ƒuta si dzi kpewo le la ƒe nukpɔkpɔ si wota le gɔmedzedzea me. Womeŋlɔ nutala la kple ŋkeke si dzi woŋlɔe ɖe nɔnɔmetata la ŋu o.
An early photograph of one of the toweri: Meenakshi Amman Gbedoxɔa ƒe agbo kɔkɔwo dometɔ ɖeka ƒe foto gbãtɔ, si wokpɔ tso ablɔ si le ete dzi. Womeléa fotoɖela kple ŋkeke si dzi woŋlɔe ɖe nɔnɔmetata la ŋu o.
An excavated settlement near the Vaigai: Amewo ƒe nɔƒe si woɖe le teƒe si te ɖe Vaigai ŋu le Sivaganga nutoa me, si me wotu anyikpewo, zewo kple blemanu geɖewo le.
An excavator lifts a small pot from insi: Tomenukula aɖe kɔa ze sue aɖe tso ameɖibɔ gã aɖe me. Wotsɔa zewo, agbawo kple nutsyɔnuwo dana ɖe nugoeawo me kple wo ŋu kple ame kukuwo, ɖewohĩ woléa nuɖuɖu, tsi alo vɔsawo ɖe wo me — si nye dzesi be Adichanallurtɔwo kpɔ mɔzɔzɔ si yi ŋgɔ wu ku le susu me. Le sinima la me la, hamemegã aɖe ɖe eme be wona nuwo ame kukuwo be woakpe ɖe wo ŋu le woƒe mɔ dzi: “emae nye nugoe la ƒe gɔmesese”.
An institution of the Ministry of Educat: Sukudede Dɔwɔƒe, India Dziɖuɖu, ƒe dɔwɔƒe aɖe le Chennai, si tsɔ eɖokui na be yeasrɔ̃ Tamil xoxo — gbe si blema agbalẽ blaene vɔ ɖeka, tso Tolkappiyam va ɖo Muttollayiram.
An iron blade and a knife, measured agai: Gayibɔ kple hɛ, si wodzidze ɖe nudanu dzi. Numekuku siwo ŋu woƒo nu tsoe le sinima la me ɖee fia be Adichanallur’s smiths wɔa gayibɔ si me carbon sɔ gbɔ ɖo eye wosẽnɛ to etutu me — wotsɔa ga dzodzoe la dea ami me — si nye gaŋutinunya aɖaŋutɔe kple eɖoɖo koŋ ƒe dzesi.
An old Tanjore painting of Rama’s corona: Tanjoretɔwo ƒe nutata xoxo aɖe si ɖe Rama ƒe fiakukuɖoɖo fia. An urn exposed in a trench at Sivakalai,: Nugoe aɖe si woɖe ɖe go le do aɖe me le Sivakalai, si didi tso Adichanallur gbɔ abe kilometa adre ene le Thamirabarani-tɔsisia to. Ancient and medieval Tamil irrigation sy: Tamiltɔwo ƒe tsidede agble ƒe ɖoɖo siwo nɔ anyi le blema kple titinaɣeyiɣiwo me zãa tsidoƒe siwo ŋu wotrɔ asi le nyuie tsɔ kpɔa alesi tsi zɔna tso tsigowo me yia agbledeƒewo dzi. Menye ʋuƒo siwo le aʋawɔʋu ƒe gli me koe xɔ siawo nye o; aɖaŋu vovovowo kpe ɖe tsi ƒe sisi ŋu nyuie eye woma tsi siwo wodzra ɖo ɖe agblewo me. Woŋlɔ sluice ƒomevi geɖe siwo wozãna tsã la ɖi le Tamil Nadu, siwo dometɔ aɖewoe nye madai, madagu, thumpu kple kumizhi. Woƒe aɖaŋu kple dɔwɔwɔ pɛpɛpɛ to vovo. Kpɔɖeŋu dodzidzɔname aɖe koŋ enye kumizhi ɖoɖo, si nye tsidzɔƒe tɔxɛ aɖe si do ƒome kple tsidzɔƒe-tsiwo zazã tso blema ke. Tsi si wotsɔna tsia tsii kpena ɖe agbledelawo ŋu woɖea tsi ɖa ne ehiã, tsɔ wu be woaɖe mɔ tsigoa me tsi ƒuƒlu le mɔ si dzi womeɖu o nu, eye wodoa alɔ tsi mama ɖe ɖoɖo nu to mɔ siwo subɔa agbledeƒe vovovowo dzi. Woƒe xɔtutu ɖe sidzedze ŋutɔŋutɔ si le tsi ƒe nyaƒoɖeamenu, afisi woɖea do le, nuheŋusẽ kple ƒomedodo si le nudzraɖoƒewo kple agbledenyigbawo dome fiana. Nuŋɔŋlɔ siwo gakpɔtɔ li nye kpeɖodzi vevi aɖewo koŋ na tsidede agble ƒe mɔ̃ɖaŋununya sia kple akpa si wòwɔna le agbledeƒewo ƒe nɔnɔmewo tɔtrɔ me.

At Sittanavasal in Pudukkottai district,: Le Sittanavasal le Pudukkottai nutoa me la, wota Jaintɔwo ƒe gbedoxɔ aɖe si wotsɔ kpe kpae, si nye Arivar Koil, ƒe dzisasrã abe lotus-ta ene: lotus kple liliti-tiwo, tɔmelãwo, akpɔkplɔwo, sɔwo kple nyitsuwo, kple mawusubɔla siwo le seƒoƒowo ƒom ƒu. In classical Tamil literature the five t: Le Tamiltɔwo ƒe agbalẽ xoxowo me la, tinai ƒe anyigba atɔ̃awo — Kurinji, Mullai, Marutham, Neithal kple Palai — meƒo nu tso anyigba ƒe nɔnɔme ɖeɖeko ŋu o ke woƒo nu tso amewo ƒe dɔwo, dzɔdzɔmenunɔamesiwo, seselelãmewo kple agbenɔnɔ hã ŋu. In Perundurai taluk, Erode district, Kod: Le Perundurai taluk, Erode nutoa me la, Kodumanal ɖe asitsatsa ƒe akpa si wowɔna fiana. Kallanai stands across the Kaveri about: Kallanai le Kaveri-tɔsisia ƒe go kemɛ dzi abe kilometa wuiatɔ̃ ene tso Tiruchirappalli, le Srirangam ƒukpoa ƒe ɣedzeƒe gome, afisi tɔsisia dzea mama gɔme le hena tɔʋua. Menye nudzraɖoƒee wònye o ke boŋ anicut: tsidzɔƒe si xea mɔ na tɔsisia ale gbegbe be wòte ŋu trɔa eƒe tsi wòzua tɔdzisasrãwo. Blema nuto si le eme nye gli bɔbɔe aɖe si wotsɔ kpe si wometso o si didi abe meta 330 ene; wotu tɔdzisasrã si wotsɔ aɖaka wɔe kple yadoƒe siwo wokpɔna egbea ɖe edzi le ƒe alafa wuiadelia kple blaevelia me.
Kallanai was built without mortar, on th: Wotu Kallanai aŋɔ manɔmee, ɖe tɔsisia ŋutɔ ƒe ke si le ʋuʋum la dzi. Etulawo ƒo kpe gã siwo wometso o la ƒu gbe ɖe Kaveri-tɔsisia me; esi ƒutsotsoeawo nɔ kea ƒom tso wo te la, kpeawo nyrɔ, eye bubuwo ƒo ƒu ɖe wo dzi vaseɖe esime kpeawo va nɔ anyigba sesẽ dzi. Anyigba kple tsiɖɔɖɔa ƒe tsikpewo yɔ doawo me eye wobla kpeawo wozu mɔxenu ɖeka si me tsi mate ŋu age ɖo o: gli gbadza si keke si didi abe meta 330 ene eye wòkeke abe meta 20 ene, si wotsɔ mlɔ fli si le tsatsam si nuŋlɔɖia tsɔ sɔ kple da si le tsatsam la me. Enye anicut, ke menye tsita o — ekɔa tɔsisia ɖe dzi ale gbegbe be wòaɖo eƒe tsi ɖe tɔdzisasrãwo me, eye wònana susɔeawo toa eme.
Kallanai, also known as the Grand Anicut: Kallanai, si wogayɔna be Grand Anicut, nye tsi ƒe mɔ̃ɖaŋununya deŋgɔ ƒe kpɔɖeŋu ɖedzesitɔwo dometɔ ɖeka le Tamil Nadu. Etsi tre ɖe Kaveri Tɔsisia ƒe go kemɛ dzi eye tso blema ke la, wogblɔna be Karikala Chola, si nye Cholatɔwo ƒe fia gbãtɔ aɖe, gbɔe wòtso. Wotrɔ asi le xɔa ŋu koŋ be wòatrɔ tɔsisi me tsi ayi tsidedee ƒe mɔwo dzi tsɔ wu be wòadzra tsi ɖo ɖe tsidzraɖoƒe ko. Tɔdzisasrãa kpe ɖe Kaveri ƒe tsiwo mama ŋu le agbledenyigba nyui siwo le tɔʋua ƒe golɔgoewo me, afisi bligbledede va le vevie ŋutɔ le. Eƒe kpe gbadza si le bɔbɔe la wɔa dɔ kple tɔsisia ƒe sisi tsɔ fiaa mɔ tsi yia tsidede agble ƒe mɔnuwo gbɔ. To vovo na egbegbe tɔdzisasrã kɔkɔ aɖe la, eƒe taɖodzinu vevitɔe nye tsi ƒe mɔ bubu kple emama. Kallanai tsi tre ɖi na ƒomedodo kplikplikpli si le tɔsisiwo dzi kpɔkpɔ, agbledede ƒe nuwɔwɔ kple amewo ƒe nɔƒe le Tamil nutoa me dome. Akpa si wòyi edzi wɔna le tsidede agble ƒe ɖoɖoa me hã ɖe alesi mɔ̃ɖaŋudɔwɔƒe xoxowo ate ŋu akpɔtɔ anye viɖenu to beléle na wo emegbe kple tɔtrɔ ɖe nɔnɔmewo ŋu me la fia. Togbɔ be kakaɖedzi mele ɣeyiɣi si tututu wotue gbã ŋu o hã la, edo ƒome kple Cholatɔwo ƒe ɣeyiɣia ƒe gɔmedzedze le afisiafi.

Keezhadi demonstrates how archaeology ca: Keezhadi ɖe alesi blematomenukulawo ate ŋu ana míaƒe gɔmesese nade to ɖe edzi le blema Tamiltɔwo ƒe hadomegbenɔnɔ ŋu wu nusi agbalẽŋɔŋlɔwo ɖeɖe ate ŋu agblɔ na mí la fia.
Keezhadi is an important archaeological: Keezhadi nye blematomenukuƒe vevi aɖe si te ɖe Vaigai Tɔsisi ŋu le Sivaganga nutoa me. Tomenukukuwo ke ɖe xɔtuɖaŋu ƒe kpeƒekpeƒewo, zewo, blemanuwo kple kpeɖodzi bubu siwo fia be woɖoe ɖe ɖoɖo nu ŋu. Nusiwo ŋu woke ɖo siawo kpena ɖe dugãwo me nɔnɔ, ŋutilãme dekɔnuwo kple gbesiagbegbenɔnɔ ŋuti nusɔsrɔ̃ le blema Tamil nutoa me ŋu. Nusiwo ŋu blematomenukulawo ke ɖo la xɔ asi ŋutɔ elabena wonaa ŋutilãmenu siwo ŋu woate ŋu asrɔ̃ nu tsoe kpe ɖe Tamiltɔwo ƒe agbalẽŋɔŋlɔ ƒe kɔnyinyiwo ŋu. Gake ele be woaɖe ame siwo nɔ afima ƒe amenyenye tututu, hadomeɖoɖowɔwɔ kple ŋutinya bliboa gɔme tso kpeɖodzi siwo li me.

Koozh is a traditional porridge prepared: Koozh nye mɔli si wozãna le blema si wotsɔa nukuwo abe millet ene ɖana, eye wozãa nuku siwo wotsɔ ƒo ƒu wɔe le eƒe akpa aɖewo me. Enaa mɔnu nyui aɖe si dzi woato atsɔ nusiwo le nutoa me aɖa nuɖuɖu si me wodea nuɖuɖui. Ɣeyiɣi didi aɖee nye sia si wotsɔ nukumɔli do ƒome kple gbesiagbe nuɖuɖu ƒe kɔnyinyiwo le Tamil nutoawo me, togbɔ be nuɖaɖa tɔxɛwo kple nusiwo wotsɔ wɔe to vovo hã.
Korkai, Alagankulam, Puhar, Arikamedu an: Korkai, Alagankulam, Puhar, Arikamedu kple Muziris — le fotogbalẽ siwo me woɖe tomenuawo le me.
Krishna — often shown in Tanjore paintin: Krishna — si woɖena fiana zi geɖe le Tanjore ƒe nutatawo me abe ɖevi si fi bɔta ene, alo abe nyikplɔla si tsɔa eƒe saŋku ene — nɔ Thanjavur nutalawo ƒe nyati siwo wolɔ̃na wu le Maratha-fiawo ƒe dziɖuɣi la dome. Eƒe ŋutigbalẽ ɣi, sika ƒe atsyɔ̃ɖonuwo kple fiakuku si wotsɔ kpe xɔasiwo wɔe la dzena le megbenyawo ƒe amadede siwo le keklẽm eye wole gbadzaa la me.
Krishna with Radha, his beloved, a favou: Krishna kple Radha, eƒe lɔlɔ̃tɔ, si nye ɖokuitsɔtsɔna ƒe nutata ƒe nyati si wòlɔ̃na wu. Tanjore nutalawo ɖea mawume atsu kple asi siwo do awu nyuie eye wotsɔ kpe xɔasiwo ɖo wo ŋu la fiana le aɖaka aɖe te, woƒe atsyɔ̃ɖonuwo kɔ ɖe dzi le gesso me eye wotsɔ sika ɖo wo ŋu ale be woaklẽ le akaɖia ƒe keklẽ me.

Kurinji — mountains, union of lovers. Mu: Kurinji — towo, lɔlɔ̃tɔwo ƒe ɖekawɔwɔ. Mullai — avewo, dzigbɔɖi le lala. Marutham — agbledenyigba, lɔlɔ̃tɔwo ƒe dzrewɔwɔ. Neythal — ƒuta, dzimaɖitsitsi didi. Palai — anyigba ƒuƒui, mama. Anyigba ƒe nɔnɔme ɖesiaɖe tsɔa eƒe ɣeyiɣi, ŋkekea ƒe ɣeyiɣi, seƒoƒowo, xeviwo, kple mawuwo, si naa nɔnɔmetatawo ƒe nyagbe gbogbo aɖewo siwo wozãna ɖekae la nɔa hakpanyaawo me.
Kurinji represents mountainous regions w: Kurinji tsi tre ɖi na tonyigba siwo dzi adedada, avemenukuwo nuƒoƒoƒu kple nuku siwo sɔ agbledede nye mɔ vevi siwo dzi woato akpɔ nuɖuɖu le. Tamilgbe me nuŋlɔɖi xoxowo do ƒome kple anyigba sia kple millet, anyitsi, gbemetitsetsewo kple nuɖuɖu siwo wokpɔna tso adedada me. Nuɖuɖu siwo do ƒome kple Kurinji: thinai (akpɔkplɔ ƒe asike), anyitsi, gbe me atikutsetsewo, bambu bli afisi bambu la se seƒoƒo le, ave me aŋgbawo kple kewo, lã siwo tso adedada me, kple amagbe kple nuku siwo woate ŋu aɖu. Nuɖuɖu ƒe nɔnɔmetata si bɔ: lãgbalẽ si me anyitsi le, atikutsetse kple ke siwo woƒo ƒu, tsɔ kpe ɖe lã si wokpɔ to adedada me ŋu.
Kurinji, Mullai, Marutham, Neithal and P: Kurinji, Mullai, Marutham, Neithal kple Palai — Tamil hakpanyawo ƒe towo, avewo, agblewo, ƒuta kple anyigba ƒuƒuiwo, wo dometɔ ɖesiaɖe kple eƒe ɣeyiɣi kple gaƒoƒo, eƒe mawuwo, seƒoƒowo kple amewo, kple lɔlɔ̃ ƒe seselelãme si wòtsɔna.
Lakshmi, goddess of prosperity, seated b: Lakshmi, nudzedziname ƒe mawunɔ, bɔbɔ nɔ sɔ eve siwo doa lotus ɖe woƒe akɔta dome — nɔnɔme si woyɔna be Gajalakshmi. Le aɖaka si wotsɔ sika wɔe si wotsɔ xɔmetsovɔ damawo ƒo ɖe edzi te la, wodo eƒe fiakuku, kpe xɔasiwo kple seƒoƒotsihewo ɖe dzi le nɔnɔmetata me eye wotsɔ sika aŋgba tsyɔ edzi, eye wotsɔ kpe dzĩ kple amadede dzẽwo ɖo xɔa me.

Madurai represents the enduring relation: Madurai tsi tre ɖi na ƒomedodo si nɔa anyi ɖaa si le Tamiltɔwo ƒe agbalẽwo, fia ƒe kpekpeɖeŋunana, mawusubɔsubɔ ƒe kɔnyinyiwo kple dugã me agbenɔnɔ dome.
Madurai was one of the most important ce: Madurai nye blema Pandya fiaɖuƒea ƒe teƒe vevitɔwo dometɔ ɖeka. Edo ƒome kplikplikpli kple Tamiltɔwo ƒe agbalẽŋɔŋlɔ ƒe kɔnyinyiwo kple Tamiltɔwo ƒe hakpanya xoxowo ƒe ŋgɔyiyi. Blema agbalẽwo gblɔ tso Madurai ŋu be enye du si me nu dze edzi na hakpanyaŋlɔlawo, agbalẽnyalagãwo, asitsala kple dziɖulawo ƒoa ƒu ɖo. Dua wɔ akpa vevi aɖe le asitsatsa, mawusubɔsubɔ ƒe agbenɔnɔ kple dekɔnuwo ƒe asitɔtrɔ hã me. Togbɔ be blema Madurai ŋuti numeɖeɖewo gakpɔtɔ le agbalẽwo me hã la, womate ŋu agbugbɔ eƒe dzedzeme tututu le Sangam ƒe ɣeyiɣia me aɖo kpe edzi bliboe o.
Mamallapuram showcases the creativity, c: Mamallapuram ɖea nutovɛ, asinudɔwɔwɔ kple xɔtuɖaŋu yeye siwo wowɔ le Pallava ɣeyiɣia me fiana.
Mamallapuram, also known as Mahabalipura: Mamallapuram, si wogayɔna be Mahabalipuram, va zu Pallavatɔwo ƒe aɖaŋudɔwo kple xɔtuɖaŋu ƒe teƒe vevi aɖe. Pallava dziɖulawo do alɔ agado siwo wotso kpewo, ŋkuɖodzinu siwo wotu ɖe kpe ɖeka dzi, kpememewo kple xɔtuƒewo wɔwɔ. Eƒe ŋkuɖodzinu siwo woɖua azã na wu dometɔ aɖewoe nye Ratha Atɔ̃awo, Ƒuta Gbedoxɔa, kple kpememe gã si woyɔna zi geɖe be Arjuna’s Penance alo Descent of the Ganges. Dɔ siawo ɖe Pallava aɖaŋudɔwɔlawo ƒe aɖaŋu kple xɔtuɖaŋu tɔxɛwo toto vɛ fia.

Manimegalai by Seethalai Sathanar, one o: Manimegalai si Seethalai Sathanar ŋlɔ, si nye Epic Gã Atɔ̃awo dometɔ ɖeka eye wònye Silapathikaram ƒe ŋgɔdonya. Ekplɔ Manimegalai, si nye Kovalan kple Madhavi vinyɔnu, ɖo le eƒe mɔ si dzi wòto va zu Buddhatɔwo ƒe nyɔnu saɖagaxɔmenɔla la dzi.

Many coins of this period come from rive: Ɣeyiɣi sia me gaku geɖe tso tɔsisiwo kple tomenukuƒewo, afisi ƒe alafa geɖe ƒe vuvu na woƒe atsyãwo fa. Zi geɖe la, wo xexlẽ nɔ te ɖe lã ƒomevi ɖeka ƒe kpɔɖeŋu geɖe tsɔtsɔ sɔ kple wo nɔewo dzi.

Marutham represents fertile agricultural: Marutham tsi tre ɖi na agbledeƒe nyuiwo, vevietɔ teƒe siwo sɔ na bligbledede. Agbledede doa alɔ nuto siwo me amewo va nɔ, eye nuku siwo wode agble ɖe wo dzi ƒe amesinɔnɔ na be woate ŋu aɖu nu vovovowo. Nuɖuɖu siwo do ƒome kple Marutham: bli, bli, amagbe kple amagbe siwo wozãna le ɣeyiɣi aɖe me, sukli me tsi kple nu viviwo, tɔmelã siwo tso tɔsisiwo kple tsitawo me, lã le nutoa me tɔwo ƒe nya nu, atikutsetsewo, kple sesame kple eƒe ami. Nuɖuɖu ƒe nɔnɔmetata si bɔ: bli si woɖa si wotsɔa nukuwo, amagbewo kple, afisi woate ŋu akpɔe le la, tɔmelã alo lã ɖana.
Material evidence of urban life that can: Dugã me agbenɔnɔ ŋuti kpeɖodzi ŋutɔŋutɔ siwo woate ŋu asrɔ̃ kpe ɖe Sangamtɔwo ƒe agbalẽwo ŋu.
Mats were woven from materials such as p: Wotsɔa nusiwo le abe deti ƒe aŋgbawo, aŋgbawo kple gbewo ene lɔ̃a matwo. Wozãa wo tsɔ nɔa anyi, mlɔa anyi, ɖiɖina ɖe eme kple amedzrowo xɔxɔ. Le nusi wotsɔ wɔe kple avɔlɔlɔ̃ ƒe mɔnu nu la, matwo ƒe nɔnɔme, woƒe lolome kple woƒe anyinɔnɔ le vovovo. Woate ŋu aƒo wo nu ƒu ahadzra wo ɖo ne womele wo zãm o, si wɔnɛ be woate ŋu azã wo le gbesiagbegbenɔnɔ me.

Millets were important grains, particula: Milets nye nuku veviwo, vevietɔ le nuto siwo me tsidzadza kple anyigba ƒe nɔnɔmewo doa dzidzɔ na wo le. Woate ŋu aɖa thinai (akpɔkplɔ ƒe asike), varagu (kodo-mi) kple kambu (dzonu ƒuƒu) abe nukuwo ene, awɔe wòanye mɔli alo aɖae le nɔnɔme bubuwo me. Woƒe vevienyenye ɖe alesi nuɖuɖu ƒe nɔnɔmewo trɔ ɖe nutoa me ƒe nɔnɔmewo nu fia.
Modern Kanchipuram is widely known as a: Wonya egbegbe Kanchipuram le afisiafi be enye gbedoxɔdu kple seda ƒe avɔlɔ̃ƒe vevi aɖe. Eƒe ŋutinya me gbedoxɔwo yi edzi nye tadeaguƒewo, evɔ seda saree siwo wozãna tsã la doa ka kple dua kple asinudɔwɔwɔ ƒe domenyinu si li tso gbaɖegbe ke. Amedzrowo ate ŋu akpɔ eƒe mawusubɔsubɔ ƒe xɔtuɖaŋu, nutoa me asiwo kple dekɔnu ƒe nuwɔna gbagbewo.
Modern Poompuhar is a coastal settlement: Egbegbe Poompuhar nye ƒutadu aɖe le Mayiladuthurai nuto me, Tamil Nadu. Ƒuta, nutoa me tɔwo, dekɔnu dɔwɔƒewo kple blematomenukulawo ƒe numekukuwo kpɔa eƒe kadodo kple blema Tamiltɔwo ƒe ƒudziŋutinya ta. Tɔtrɔ siwo va le ƒuta kple anyigba ƒe ʋuʋu gblẽ nu le anyigba ƒe nɔnɔme ŋu, eye womenya alesi blema melidzeƒedu la nɔ bliboe kple kakaɖedzi o.
Modern Thanjavur remains a major cultura: Egbegbe Thanjavur gakpɔtɔ nye dekɔnuwo ƒe teƒe vevi aɖe le Tamil Nadu. Brihadisvara Gbedoxɔa yi edzi le tadeagulawo, ŋutinyaŋlɔlawo, xɔtuɖaŋunyalawo kple tsaɖilawo hem vɛ. Wonya dua hã ɖe Thanjavur nutatawo, blema hadzidziwo, ɣeɖuɖu, akɔblikpakpawo kple dekɔnu asinudɔwɔwɔwo ta.

Mullai represents pastoral and woodland: Mullai tsi tre ɖi na lãnyinyi kple avenyigba siwo do ƒome kple nyinyinyi kple lãnyilawo ƒe agbenɔnɔ. Notsi kple nyinotsinuwo nye nuɖuɖu veviwo, gake wokpɔa nukuwo kple nu bubuwo to agbledede, wo ɖɔliɖɔli kple nutoa me nuƒoƒoƒu me. Nuɖuɖu siwo do ƒome kple Mullai: notsi (paal), curd (thayir), bɔta (mor), bɔta (vennai), thinai kple varagu millets, bli kple nuku bubu siwo wokpɔ to agbledede alo wo ɖɔliɖɔli me, eye le nuto aɖewo me la, lã. Nuɖuɖu ƒe nɔnɔmetata si bɔ: bli alo bli si wotsɔa lãmi alo bɔta kpena ɖe eŋu, eye notsi kple nyinotsi bubuwo hã le eme abe nuɖuɖu veviwo ene.
Munrurai Araiyanar’s four hundred verses: Munrurai Araiyanar ƒe kpukpui alafa ene, siwo dometɔ ɖesiaɖe wu enu ɖe ​​lododo aɖe dzi.
Nakkeerar’s guide-poem directing a devot: Nakkeerar ƒe mɔfiame-hakpanya si fia mɔ subɔla aɖe yi Murugan ƒe gbedoxɔ adeawo me, si wogbugbɔ ŋlɔ kple Nachinarkkiniyar ƒe numeɖeɖe.
Nakkeerar’s poem of the long, cold north: Nakkeerar ƒe hakpanya si ku ɖe dzieheya didi si fa miamiamia ŋu: fianyɔnu aɖe si medɔa alɔ̃ o le eƒe fiasã me esime fia la le adzɔge le aʋawɔwɔ me.
Naladiyar: 400 four-line verses on ethic: Naladiyar: Kpukpui 400 siwo me fli ene le siwo ƒo nu tso agbenyuinɔnɔ ŋu, siwo wogblɔna tso blema ke be Jain saɖagaxɔmenɔlawoe ŋlɔe. Wodea asixɔxɔ eŋu ale gbegbe be Tamilgbe me lododo aɖe tsɔe kpe ɖe Thirukkuralgbe ŋu be: “Naalum irandum sollukku urudhi.”
Nallathanar’s hundred verses, each namin: Nallathanar ƒe kpukpui alafa ɖeka, siwo dometɔ ɖesiaɖe yɔ nu etɔ̃ siwo daa gbe le susu ŋu abe alesi ginger ƒuƒu, atadi kple atadi didi daa gbe le ŋutilã ŋu ene.
Nallur Nathathanar’s guide-poem sending: Nallur Nathathanar ƒe mɔfiame-hakpanya si ɖo bard dahe aɖe ɖe amegã Nalliyakkodan. Woŋlɔa kɔpi sia ɖe pepa dzi tsɔ wu be woaŋlɔe ɖe deti ƒe aŋgba dzi.
Named in Sangam poetry as a capital of t: Wotsɔ ŋkɔ nɛ le Sangam hakpanyawo me be enye Chola gbãtɔwo ƒe fiadu; egbea enye Tiruchirappalli dugã la ƒe akpa aɖe.

Near the mouth of the Kaveri, Puhar is r: Le Kaveri-tɔsisia ƒe nugbɔ gbɔ la, woɖoa ŋku Puhar dzi be enye Cholatɔ gbãtɔwo ƒe melidzeƒedu gã, si doa ka kple bligblewo, tsimɔwo kple asiwo le Kaveri-tɔsisia ƒe golɔgoewo me kple Bengal-ƒuta. Near the Tamiraparani in Thoothukudi dis: Le Tamiraparani gbɔ le Thoothukudi nutoa me la, Korkai nye Pandya melidzeƒe si le Mannar-ƒuta ƒe dzonu lãɖeɖe — ganya si me tsi me nɔnɔ, ʋuʋu kple ƒumelãwo ƒe vovototodedeameme, dzonuwo ƒe hatsotsowo me toto kple wo dzadzra. Neithal represents coastal regions where: Neithal tsi tre ɖi na ƒuta nuto siwo me tɔƒodede, dzewɔwɔ kple ƒudzidɔwo nɔ vevie le. Nuɖuɖu siwo do ƒome kple Neithal: tɔmelã yeyewo, tɔmelã ƒuƒu (karuvadu), lãgbalẽgolo, kpakpaluʋui kple lãgbalẽ, dze si tso ƒuta dzezewo me, bli to agbledede alo asitsatsa me, koklozi, kple ƒumelã siwo woɖa kple nutoa me nu ʋeʋĩwo. Nuɖuɖu ƒe nɔnɔmetata si bɔ: tɔmelã alo tɔmelã ƒuƒu si wotsɔ bli ɖae, kple ƒumelã bubuwo kple nutoa me nuɖuɖuwo.

On a low gravel mound on the south bank: Le kpe gbadzɛ aɖe si le Thamirabarani-tɔsisia ƒe dzigbeƒuta, si didi tso Tirunelveli gbɔ abe kilometa 24 ene le Thoothukudi nutoa me la, ameɖibɔ gãtɔ kekeake siwo nɔ anyi le India le ŋutinya gbãtɔ me la dometɔ ɖeka le, eye wòkeke ɖe enu wu acre alafa ɖeka. Woɖi nugoe akpe geɖe ɖe afisia, zi geɖe la, woblaa wo ɖe wo nɔewo gbɔ, eye wotsɔa amegbetɔ ƒe kuku siwo me gayibɔdɔwɔnuwo kple aʋawɔnuwo, akɔbligowo kple kpememewo, sikafiakukuwo, dzonu kple ze siwo ƒe amadede nye yevu kple dzĩ la nɔa wo me. Wodze tomenukuku gɔme le ƒe 1876 me, le Indiatɔwo ƒe blematomenukulawo ƒe gbãtɔwo dome, eye fifia ƒe ɣeyiɣi siwo wotsɔ radiocarbon wɔe la ɖee fia be ameɖiawo nɔ ƒe akpe gbãtɔ D.M.Ŋ. Wokpɔ nɔƒe aɖe si me zemela ƒe dzodoƒe le le afima te ɖe afima ŋu: ame siwo ɖi woƒe ame kukuwo ɖe afisia hã nɔa wo xa, dea agble hewɔa gadɔ.
On the Amaravathi river, Karur — remembe: Le Amaravathi tɔsisia dzi la, Karur — si dzi woɖoa ŋkui be Vanchi kple Karuvur — nye anyigba ƒe titina si do ƒome kple Chera-fiawo. Karur mlɔ mɔ siwo anya do ƒome kple ɣetoɖoƒe kple ɣedzeƒeƒuta, ɖo ta Muziris kple Arikamedu dzi; eƒe Romatɔwo ƒe gakuwo ɖea ga ƒe kadodo fiana, gake menye asitsatsa kple Roma tẽ kokoko o.
On the banks of the Thamirabarani in Tho: India ƒe Gaɣeyiɣia me ameɖiƒe gãwo dometɔ ɖeka le Thamirabarani-tɔsisia to le Thoothukudi nutoa me. Woku Adichanallur zi gbãtɔ le ƒe 1876 me eye Alexander Rea ye kue le ƒe 1899 kple 1905 dome, eye India ƒe Blemanuwo Ŋuti Numekuƒe gakue tso ƒe 2004 me, eye wokpɔ nugoe gã siwo me amegbetɔ ƒe kukuawo le, siwo wotsɔ gayibɔdɔwɔnuwo kple aʋawɔnuwo ɖo, akɔbligowo, atsyɔ̃ɖonuwo kple sika nu me-kawo. Sangam hakpanyawo ƒoa nu tso nugoe mawo tɔgbe ŋu — முதுமக்கள் தாழி — eye woƒoa nu na zemela si wɔ wo gɔ̃ hã be: கலம்செய் கோவே, “Oo fia le wo dome zemelawo”.
On the Malabar coast of present-day Kera: Le Malabar ƒuta le egbegbe Kerala la, Muziris nye melidzeƒe gã aɖe si India-ƒua ƒe asitsatsa le gɔmedzedzea me, si xɔ ŋkɔ le atadi ta gake edzrana wu kura: ave kple agblemenuku siwo tso megbenyigbawo dzi, zewo kple ze nyui siwo wotsɔ tso duta vɛ, kple adzɔnu siwo asitsalawo tsɔna yia nuto geɖe me. Erythraean Ƒua ƒe Periplus tsɔe da ɖe melidzeƒe siwo do ƒome kple Ƒudzĩa, Egipte kple Mediterranea-ƒua ƒe kadodo aɖe me. Woʋlia nya le teƒe si tututu wòle ŋu: tomenukuku le Pattanam ɖe zemela kple ʋutsɔze siwo wotsɔ tso duta vɛ fia, eye Pattanam ate ŋu anye blema Muziritɔwo ƒe akpa aɖe — agbalẽnyalagãwo ƒe nukpɔsusu aɖe, ke menye nyateƒenya si ŋu woɖo kpee o.

Sangam literature is the earliest body o: Sangam agbalẽwoe nye Tamiltɔwo ƒe hakpanyawo ƒe hatsotso gbãtɔ. Le kɔnu nu la, woƒoe nu ƒu ɖe nuƒoƒoƒu gã eve me: Eight Anthologies (Ettuthokai) kple Ten Idylls (Pattuppattu). Wo katã wodzra hakpanyaŋlɔla alafa geɖe ƒe hakpanya siwo wu akpe eve ɖo, siwo dometɔ aɖewoe nye nyɔnuwo, fiawo, kple hakpanyaŋlɔla siwo le tsaglãla tsam.
Sangam poems already speak of painters a: Sangam hakpanyawo ƒo nu tso nutala kple akpata siwo wota ŋu xoxo: ஓவியர் siwo tsɔa fli nyuiwo taa nu, kple ஓவியச் செந்நூல், si nye nutata ŋuti agbalẽ. Nusiwo gakpɔtɔ le gliwo dzi dze egɔme tso ƒe alafa 7 lia–9 lia me — le Pallava gbedoxɔwo kple Jaintɔwo ƒe agado si le Sittanavasal me — eye wòto Cholatɔwo ƒe gli gã siwo le Thanjavur me va ɖo Nayaktɔwo ƒe glitata siwo le keklẽm kple Tanjore-kpe siwo wotsɔ sika wɔe le ƒe alafa 17 lia–19 lia me. Wotsɔ tomenu kple numiemie ƒe amadedewo — ochre dzĩ kple ɣi, akaɖi yibɔ, lime ɣi, anyigba dama — da ɖe lime plaster dzi le kɔnyinyi si nɔ anyi ƒe akpe ɖeka kple edzivɔ me.
Sangam poems are classed as akam (the in: Wobua Sangam hakpanyawo ɖe hatsotso me be akam (lɔlɔ̃ ƒe xexe ememetɔ) alo puram (aʋa, fiaɖuƒe, dɔmenyonyo, kple agbenyuinɔnɔ ƒe gotagome xexe). Akam hakpanyawo meyɔa woƒe lɔlɔ̃tɔwo ŋkɔ gbeɖe o; woƒoa nu to ƒomeviwo dzi — kalẽtɔ, kalẽtɔ, xɔlɔ̃, vidada si xɔe nyi.

Sesame was cultivated and used as a food: Wodea sesame eye wozãnɛ abe nuɖuɖu ene. Woate ŋu atsɔ sesame-ku ade nusiwo woɖana me, gake sesame-mi ya nyea nuɖanu eye wozãnɛ le blema ke. Amiwɔwɔ hã ɖea sidzedze si le nukuwo ŋudɔwɔwɔ ŋu be woakpɔ aƒemenuzazã siwo ŋu viɖe le la fiana.
Seventy akam verses by Moovathiyar, four: Akam kpukpui blaadre siwo Moovathiyar ŋlɔ, wuiene na anyigba ƒe nɔnɔme atɔ̃awo dometɔ ɖesiaɖe; kpukpui ʋɛ aɖewo bu.
Several works of the Eighteen Minor Clas: Nuŋlɔɖi Sue Wuiatɔ̃awo ƒe agbalẽ geɖe (Pathinenkilkanakku) ɖo woƒe kpukpuiwo ɖe ɖoɖo nu le anyigba ƒe nɔnɔme nu: Aintinai Aimpathu kple Tinaimozhi Aimpathu na kpukpui ewo na tinai ɖesiaɖe, Aintinai Ezhupathu wuiene, eye Tinaimalai Nurraimpathu na abe blaetɔ̃ ene; Kainnilai hã kplɔa anyigba atɔ̃awo ɖo. Le Sangam ƒe agbalẽ siwo woƒo ƒu dome la, Ainkurunuru tsɔ hakpanya kpui alafa ɖeka na wo dometɔ ɖesiaɖe. Afisiae wole le deti ƒe aŋgba ƒe babla siwo me wogbugbɔ wo kɔpi le hedzra ɖo me — ɖe babla aɖe be wòatrɔ eƒe aŋgbawo.
Shaiva poet-saint · 7th century CE: Shaiva hakpanyaŋlɔla-ame kɔkɔe · ƒe alafa 7 lia M.Ŋ
Sherds of rouletted ware from Arikamedu,: Nu siwo wotsɔ lãgbalẽ wɔe ƒe kakɛ siwo tso Arikamedu, si te ɖe Ariyankuppam ŋu, siwo India ƒe Blemanuwo Ŋuti Numekuƒe ɖe fia. Ze nyui sia si ƒe amadede nye aŋutiɖiɖi-yibɔ, si me ʋuʋudedi suesuesue siwo wotsɔ tasiaɖamfɔ si ŋu aɖu le te mi ɖe eme la le ŋutinya me teƒe gbãtɔ geɖe siwo ƒo xlã Bengal-ƒuta; wogale dɔ wɔm tso afisi wowɔe le ŋu kokoko.
Shiva and Parvati seated together as Uma: Shiva kple Parvati bɔbɔ nɔ anyi ɖekae abe Umamaheshvara ene, le seƒoƒo ƒe alɔ aɖe te. Shiva, si nye dzinu si le abe dzinuvi ene le eƒe taɖa me, lé gbetedzia eye wòdo asi ɖe dzi tsɔ yayrae; Parvati si ƒe ŋutigbalẽ le blɔ la tsia tre ɖe eŋu kplikplikpli. Atsu kple asi mawuwo ƒe atsu kple asi vividoɖeameŋutɔe nye nyati si Nayak-ɣeyiɣia me nutalawo lɔ̃na wu.
Shiva kple Parvati tsi tre ɖe wo nɔewo xa. Atsu kple asi abe esia ene nye amehawo ƒe nɔnɔmetatawo: lug siwo le woƒe gɔmeɖoanyiwo dzi tsɔa ati siwo dzi wotsɔa wo toa gbedoxɔa ƒe ablɔwo dzi le azãɖuɣiwo, eye wodoa seda, seƒoƒo kple kpe xɔasiwo.
Shiva as Dakshinamurthy, the teacher who: Shiva si nye Dakshinamurthy, si nye nufiala si fiaa nu le ɖoɖoezizi me, bɔbɔ nɔ agakpe aɖe dzi le banyan gã aɖe te, eye amegãxi ƒe ŋutigbalẽ le eƒe klowo dzi, esime nunyala tsitsi ene dze klo ɖe eƒe afɔ nu. Bosowo, akpɔkplɔwo, akpakpawo kple akpɔkplɔwo ƒoa zi ɖe alɔawo dzi. Tamil hakpanyaŋlɔlawo yɔa nɔnɔme sia tso gbaɖegbe ke be ஆலமர் செல்வன் — “aƒetɔ si nɔa banyan te”.
Shiva as Dakshinamurti, the supreme teac: Shiva abe Dakshinamurti, nufiala gãtɔ ene, si bɔbɔ nɔ banyan-ti aɖe te eye wòdze ŋgɔ dzigbe gome, hele nu fiam nunyalawo le ɖoɖoezizi me; eƒe afɔ nɔa manyamanya ƒe suetɔ dzi. Le Chola gbedoxɔwo me la, eƒe nɔnɔmetata xɔa kɔkɔeƒea ƒe gli si dze ŋgɔ dzigbe gome.
Shiva as Mahesha, the Great Lord. Chola: Shiva abe Mahesha, Aƒetɔ Gã la ene. Chola nɔnɔmetatawɔlawo ɖe Shiva fia le nɔnɔme gbogbo aɖewo me — ɣeɖula, nufiala, gbɔgbɔ vɔ̃wo tsɔtsrɔ̃la, srɔ̃nyɔnu lɔ̃ame — wo dometɔ ɖesiaɖe kple eƒe nɔnɔme, aʋawɔnuwo kple nɔnɔme siwo woɖo ɖe Agamas kple Silpa Sastras me.
Shiva as Pashupati, Lord of all creature: Shiva abe Pashupati, nuwɔwɔwo katã ƒe Aƒetɔ ene. Le Shaiva susu me la, luʋɔ lae nye pashu, si pasha bla, xexeame ƒe kɔsɔkɔsɔwo, eye Shiva nye pati — Aƒetɔ si ɖea asi le eŋu; susua le Tamil Shaiva Siddhanta ƒe dzime.
Shiva as Tripurantaka, destroyer of the: Shiva abe Tripurantaka, si gblẽa du etɔ̃ siwo dzona le asurawo me ene. Etsɔa alɔnu geɖe eye wòsẽa ŋuta, eye wòhea dati, eye wòdoa sikatasiaɖam si Brahma si ta ene le, eƒe sɔwo le ti kpom ɖo ta du sesẽawo gbɔ. Ŋutinya la — si wodzi le Tevaram, afisi Shiva nye amesi tɔ dzo du etɔ̃awo le — nye nyati si ŋu Cholatɔwo ƒe glitoto gãtɔ kekeake siwo le Gbedoxɔ Gã si le Thanjavur me le.

Shiva abe Tripurantaka, gbɔgbɔ vɔ̃wo ƒe du etɔ̃ siwo dzona la tsɔla ene, si wòtɔ dzoe kple aŋutrɔ ɖeka. Chola akɔbliwo ɖenɛ fiana le aŋutrɔdala ƒe nɔnɔme me — dati la ŋutɔ bu fifia — zi geɖe kple srɔ̃a Tripurasundari.
Shiva as vanquisher of the three cities: Shiva abe du etɔ̃awo dzi ɖula ene (Shiva Tripuravijaya) .
Shiva dances the Urdhva Tandava, one leg: Shiva ɖua Urdhva Tandava, eƒe afɔ ɖeka ƒua gbe ɖe eƒe ta si wotsɔ fiakuku ɖo la xa, eƒe asi gbogboawo léa akplɔ etɔ̃, kpẽ kple gbetedzi si le ti kpom la ɖe asi, esime Brahma si ƒe mo ene kple mawu bubu siwo wotsɔ fiakuku ɖo la le ekpɔm. Wotae le nɔnɔme yibɔ sesẽ aɖe me eye wotsɔe mlɔ anyigba dzẽ kple ɣie le anyigba dzĩ goglo aɖe dzi. Nɔnɔmea ɖo ŋku ɣeɖuɖu ƒe hoʋiʋli si wowɔ le Thiruvalangadu dzi, afisi Shiva kɔ eƒe afɔ ɖe dzi yi dziƒo — afɔɖeɖe si Kali mete ŋu sɔ kplii o.
Shiva Embracing His Consort, Uma: Shiva Kpla asi kɔ na Srɔ̃a, Uma
Shiva tenderly embracing Uma (Parvati) —: Shiva kpla asi kɔ na Uma (Parvati) vividoɖeameŋutɔe — Alingana-murti la. Nɔnɔmetata mawo ɖua mawume srɔ̃tɔawo kple Shiva kple eƒe ŋusẽ, Shakti, ƒe ɖekawɔwɔ ƒe azã; Cholatɔwo ƒe akɔbliwɔlawo na vividoɖeameŋu kple ƒomedodo kplikplikpli si ƒã hafi wosɔna le aɖaŋudɔ kɔkɔewo me la nɔa wo dome.

Silapathikaram, “the tale of the anklet”: Silapathikaram, “afɔkpodzi ƒe ŋutinya”, si Ilango Adigal ŋlɔ — Tamilgbe me Nyakpakpa Gã Atɔ̃awo dometɔ ɖeka. Egblɔ Kannagi kple Kovalan ƒe ŋutinya le Puhar, Madurai, kple Chera-nyigba dzi.

Sita, heroine of the Ramayana. Chola wor: Sita, Ramayana ƒe kalẽtɔ. Chola dɔwɔƒewo tsɔ akɔbli ƒe hatsotso siwo nye Rama, Lakshmana, Sita kple Hanuman ƒu gbe na Vishnu gbedoxɔwo; Sita tsi tre nyuie le nɔnɔme si me wòbɔbɔ zi etɔ̃ (tribhanga) me, eye zi geɖe la, etrɔna vie ɖe Rama ŋu.
Sivakalai, near Adichanallur · from the: Sivakalai, si te ɖe Adichanallur · ŋu tso sinima la me
Sixty akam verses by Pullankadanar, twel: Akam kpukpui blaade siwo Pullankadanar ŋlɔ, wuieve na anyigba ƒe nɔnɔme ɖesiaɖe; akpa aɖe koe wo dometɔ geɖe tsina.
Sixty sutras on the grammar of love poet: Sutra blaade siwo ku ɖe lɔlɔ̃hakpanyawo ƒe gbeŋutise ŋu, eye wogblɔ be Nakkeerar ye ŋlɔ numeɖeɖea si gblɔ Sangam etɔ̃awo ƒe xotutu.
Sollathikaram, the second book of the To: Sollathikaram, Tolkappiyam ƒe agbalẽ evelia: Tamilgbe me nyawo ƒe gbeŋutise, woƒe hatsotsowo, kple wo zazã.
Son of Rajaraja I. His northern expediti: Rajaraja I. Viŋutsu Eƒe dziehe mɔzɔzɔa ɖo Ganges, si na wotsɔ ŋkɔ nɛ be Gangaikonda Chola; me lɔƒo la, eƒe ƒudzisrafowo dze Srivijaya fiaɖuƒea ƒe melidzeƒewo dzi le Anyieheɣedzeƒe Asia. Eɖo fiadu yeye aɖe, si nye Gangaikondacholapuram, kple eƒe Shiva gbedoxɔ gã la.

South of Puducherry, on the Ariyankuppam: Le Puducherry ƒe dzigbe gome, le Ariyankuppam tɔsisia to la, Arikamedu nye melidzeƒe si amewo sɔ gbɔ ɖo le Ɣeyiɣi Ðeka ƒe ɣeyiɣia ƒe gɔmedzedze lɔƒo, eye ame geɖe de dzesii be enye “Poduke” si nye Helatɔwo ƒe tɔdziʋumɔfiala, si nye Periplus si le Erythraean Ƒua me. Mortimer Wheeler ye kue le ƒe 1945 me eye ƒuƒoƒo siwo va emegbe hã ku eme, eye wòkpɔ Romatɔwo ƒe amphorae siwo tsɔa wein kple amititsetse ƒe ami, Arretine kplɔ̃dzivɔ siwo le dzo dam siwo dzi woŋlɔ eƒe Italytɔwo ƒe ewɔlawo ƒe ŋkɔwo ɖo, rouletted ware, glass kple bead-wɔwɔ ƒe gbeɖuɖɔwo — kpeɖodzi si me kɔ be Tamil asitsalawo dzraa asi kple Mediterranea xexeame.

Standing Shiva and Parvati: Shiva kple Parvati siwo le tsitrenu
Steel shutters between the piers let eng: Ga siwo wotsɔ blaa tɔsisiawo dome naa mɔ̃ɖaŋudɔwɔlawo kɔa tɔsisia ɖe dzi alo ɖiɖina ɖe anyi eye wòmaa eƒe sisi me. Le ƒe 1830 me la, Aƒetɔ Arthur Cotton tu ke sitsoƒe le tɔdzisasrãa ƒe ɣedzeƒekpa dzi be yeatsɔ akɔ ke si dze tɔsisia ƒoƒo gɔme la ɖa, eye emegbe dɔwɔwɔwo tsɔ tɔdzisasrãa, yadoƒeawo kple woƒe agbowo kpee — le sinima la ƒe nya nu la, ʋɔtru blaatɔ̃ vɔ atɔ̃ siwo ŋu agbo siwo ƒe kpekpeme nye tɔn enyi le. Wotrɔ asi le tɔdzisasrã xoxoa ŋu, womeɖɔlii gbeɖe o.
Step 1 — Fibre Preparation: Cotton fibre: Afɔɖeɖe 1 — Fiber Dzadzraɖo: Woɖea kotoku me kawo ɖa le woƒe nukuwo ŋu hekɔa wo ŋu.
Step 2 — Spinning: The fibres are twiste: Afɔɖeɖe 2 — Kawo ƒoƒo: Wotsɔa lãgbalẽ alo lãgbalẽŋudɔwɔnu bubu ƒoa kaawo wozua ka.
Step 3 — Preparing the Warp: The lengthw: Afɔɖeɖe 3 — Dzadzraɖo ɖe Warp la Ŋu: Woɖoa ka siwo didi, si nye warp, la ɖe tete me le avɔlɔ̃ƒea.
Step 4 — Weaving: Crosswise weft threads: Afɔɖeɖe 4 — Avɔlɔlɔ̃: Wotsɔa ka siwo wotsɔ lãgbalẽ wɔe siwo le atitsoga la blaa avɔa kple avɔa, eye avɔa tsina.
Step 5 — Dyeing and Finishing: Depending: Afɔɖeɖe 5 — Amadede Kple Ewuwu: Le avɔa kple ɣeyiɣi si woatsɔ awɔe nu la, woate ŋu ade ama ka alo avɔ, aklɔe ahawu enu be woazã alo adzra.

Surprise me with a Kural!: Kural aɖe wɔ nuku nam ŋutɔ!
Talagirisvara Temple, Panamalai · Pallav: Talagirisvara Gbedoxɔ, Panamalai · Pallava, ƒe 1900 lɔƒo. ƒe 700 M.Ŋ
Tall two-handled amphorae, the shipping: Amphorae kɔkɔ siwo ŋu asi eve le, siwo nye Roma-xexeame ƒe meliwo, siwo wowɔ be woatsɔ wain, amititsetse ƒe ami kple tɔmelãmi to ƒu dzi. Nugo mawo ƒe kakɛ siwo le Arikamedu, Alagankulam kple Karur nye kpeɖodzi siwo me kɔ wu be Mediterranea-ƒua dzi adzɔnuwo ɖo Tamil ƒuta la dometɔ aɖewo.
Tamil farmers traditionally cultivated c: Tso blema ke la, Tamil agbledelawo dea agblemenuku siwo sɔ na anyigba vovovowo, tsidzadza ƒe ɖoɖo, kple tsizazã vovovowo. Bli nɔ vevie ŋutɔ le teƒe siwo tsi dzana le, evɔ nukuwo abe kambu kple varagu ene ya sɔ na agbledeƒe vovovo siwo me tsi medzana le o. Pulses, sesame, cotton, sugarcane, kple nuku bubuwo hã nye nutome agbledede ƒe ɖoɖowo ƒe akpa aɖe. Agbledededɔwo kplɔa ɣeyiɣi ƒe nɔnɔmewo ɖo: agbledelawo dzraa agblewo ɖo, tiaa nukuwo, ƒãa nukuwo, kpɔa tsi dzi, ɖea gbewo ɖa, eye woŋea nu le nuku ɖesiaɖe ƒe nudidiwo nu. Tsidzadza, anyigba ƒe nyonyome, kple ɣeyiɣi ƒe tɔtrɔ ŋuti sidzedze nɔ vevie ŋutɔ hafi woate ŋu awɔ ɖoɖo ɖe agbledede ŋu. Nuto vovovowo to woawo ŋutɔ ƒe nukuwo ƒe ƒuƒoƒo kple agbledede ƒe ɣletigbalẽwo vɛ. Ŋutinya me numekuku siwo wowɔ tso Sangam ƒe agbalẽwo ŋu ɖee fia be blema Tamil agbledelawo se vevienyenye si le nuku siwo sɔ tiatia kple agbledede mɔnuwo tɔtrɔ ɖe nutoa me ƒe nɔnɔmewo nu gɔme.
Tamil literature describes fine garments: Tamilgbe me agbalẽwo ƒo nu tso awu nyuiwo, avɔ siwo wotsɔ kotoklobo wɔe, avɔlɔ̃la bibiwo kple asitsatsa ŋu. Porunaratrupadai tsɔ avɔ nyuiwo sɔ kple nusiwo vivina ŋutɔ; Woyɔ Purananuru ɖe nilikachchai, si nye avɔ si do ƒome kple indigo ƒe amadede ta. Wotsɔ anyikpe de amae siwo ŋu woka nya ta le le Arikamedu kple Uraiyur la do ƒome kple ƒe alafa gbãtɔ kple evelia M.Ŋ.
Tamil poetics gives each mood of love a: Tamilgbe me hakpanyawo naa lɔlɔ̃ ƒe seselelãme ɖesiaɖe kpɔa nɔnɔme aɖe. Tolkappiyam yɔ tinai ɖesiaɖe ƒe anyigba (nilam) kple ɣeyiɣi (pozhuthu) be eƒe nu gbãtɔwo (mutharporul), eƒe mawuwo, amewo, nuɖuɖu, xeviwo, seƒoƒowo kple hadzidzi be wonye eƒe dzɔdzɔmenuwo (karupporul), eye lɔlɔ̃ ƒe akpa si wòtsɔna be enye eƒe tanya (uripporul). Seƒoƒo alo xevi ɖeka le Sangam hakpanya me sɔ gbɔ be wòaɖo nukpɔkpɔ bliboa — eye nyasela nya zi ɖeka nenye be lɔlɔ̃tɔwo do go, lala, dzre, pine alo akpa aɖe.
Tamil seafarers sailed with the monsoon: Tamil ƒudzidelawo zɔa tɔdziʋu kple tsidzadza ƒe ya siwo ƒona tso do ŋgɔ na ɣeyiɣi si bɔ. Sangam hakpanyawo ƒo nu tso Yavanatɔwo ƒe meliwo (kalam) siwo va ɖo Muziris siwo tsɔ sika eye wodzo kple atadi ŋu, eye Pattinappalaitɔwo ɖe Kaveripattinam (Puhar) melidzeƒe si amewo sɔ gbɔ ɖo la fia. Le Cholatɔwo ƒe dziɖuɣi la, ƒudziʋawɔʋuwo tso Bengal-ƒuta: Woŋlɔ Rajendra I ƒe mɔzɔzɔ yi Srivijaya, le ƒe 1025 M.Ŋ. Blema Tamiltɔwo ƒe ʋua ƒe ʋuƒo aɖeke metsi agbe bliboe o, eyata kpɔɖeŋu sia nye nutala aɖe ƒe gɔmeɖeɖe, ke menye tɔdziʋu si wonya la gbugbɔgatu o.
Tamil tradition remembers seven chieftai: Tamiltɔwo ƒe kɔnyinyi ɖoa ŋku Sangam ƒe ɣeyiɣia me amegã adre dzi wu bubuawo katã le woƒe nunana ta: Pari, Pegan, Kari, Ay Andiran, Adhiyaman, Nalli kple Ori. Nuŋlɔɖiwo kple nyatakaka tsitotsito to vovo le nuŋlɔɖiwo dome, gake ne wotsɔ wo katã ƒo ƒui la, woɖe kodai — dɔmenyonyo — fia abe dziɖula si dze ƒe dzesi ene. Woƒe nunanawo ɖua azã le kpukpui me to hakpanyaŋlɔla siwo wodo alɔe dzi, eye eyata hakpanyaawo na woƒe ŋkɔwo nɔ agbe.
Tamil-Brahmi cave records, Chola temple: Tamil-Brahmitɔwo ƒe agado me nuŋlɔɖiwo, Cholatɔwo ƒe gbedoxɔ me nuŋɔŋlɔwo, kple fia ƒe akɔbli-gbadzɛwo ƒe gakpekpeɖeŋunana.
Tamil-Brahmi inscribed potsherd: Tamil-Brahmi si woŋlɔ ɖe ze me
Tamil-Brahmi is the script of the earlie: Tamil-Brahmi ye nye Tamilgbe me nuŋɔŋlɔ gbãtɔ siwo wonya ƒe nuŋɔŋlɔ. Wo dometɔ geɖe nye nudzɔdzɔ ŋuti nuŋlɔɖi kpui siwo wokpa ɖe dzɔdzɔmedo siwo wotsɔ na asrafomegãwo ƒe tsidzadzawo kple kpe abawo dzi.

Teams of workers and elephants drag grea: Dɔwɔlawo kple sɔwo ƒe ƒuƒoƒowo hea kpe gãwo yia Kaveri gbɔ le nuwo gbugbɔgatu sia me tso sinima la me. Womezã aŋɔ aɖeke le Kallanai o: tɔdzisasrãa ƒe ŋusẽ nɔ eƒe kpe siwo wometso o ƒe lolome kple kpekpeme me. Wo ʋuʋu to lãmeka ɖeɖeko dzi nye ɖoɖowɔwɔ ƒe aʋadziɖuɖu, eye Tamiltɔwo ƒe kɔnyinyi gblɔ be Chola-fia Karikalan ƒe lɔlɔ̃nu gbɔe wòtso.
Ten decads of puram poems in praise of t: Puram hakpanya siwo woŋlɔ ƒe bla nanewo tsɔ kafu Chera-fiawo, eye wo dometɔ ɖesiaɖe ƒo nu tso fia ɖeka ŋu; ƒe bla nane gbãtɔ kple mamlɛawo bu.
Tens of thousands of Tamil palm-leaf man: Wodzraa Tamiltɔwo ƒe deti ƒe aŋgba ƒe asinuŋɔŋlɔgbalẽ akpe ewo — agbalẽwo kple gbeŋutise, gbedoxɔ me kɔnuwɔwɔ, Siddhatɔwo ƒe atikewɔwɔ, ɣletiviŋutinunya, ɣletivimefakaka, hadzidzi kple nuŋlɔɖiwo — ɖo ɖe dutoƒo nudzraɖoƒewo. The earliest Tamil dynastic coins, from: Tamil-fiaƒomea ƒe gaku gbãtɔwo, siwo tso ƒe alafa mamlɛawo D.M.Ŋ. Pandya gakuwo tsɔ sɔ kple tɔmelã si wowɔ ɖe atsyã nu; Chola gakuwo ɖea amegãxi aɖe fiana, eye zi geɖe la, sɔ alo sɔ nɔa eŋu; Chera gakuwo tsɔa dati kple aŋutrɔ. Ame aɖewo yɔa woƒe gaku siwo woɖe ɖe go la ƒe ŋkɔ le Tamil-Brahmigbe me, abe Pandya gaku siwo xlẽ பெருவழுதி (Peruvazhuthi) kple Chera-fiawo Makkotai kple Kuttuvan Kotai ƒe klosalogaku siwo wotsɔ nɔnɔmetata wɔe ene. Woɖe wo dometɔ geɖe tso Amaravathi tɔsisi si le Karur, si nye blema Cheratɔwo ƒe titina la ƒe aba dzi.
The early Pandya port near the mouth of: Pandya melidzeƒe gbãtɔ si te ɖe Thamirabarani-tɔsisia ƒe nugbɔ ŋu, si xɔ ŋkɔ le eƒe dzonu lãɖeɖe ta. Tso ɣemaɣi la, atsiaƒua ɖiɖi, si na kɔƒea va le anyigba me.

The eri system was a major part of tradi: Eri ƒe ɖoɖoa nye tsizazã deŋgɔ ƒe akpa vevi aɖe le Tamil Nadu. Eri nye tsidede agble si wowɔ be woatsɔ aƒo tsidzadza kple tsi si sina toa anyigba dzi nu ƒu ahadzrae ɖo. Le tsidzaɣi la, tsi ƒoa ƒu ɖe anyikpe aɖe megbe. Emegbe woate ŋu aɖe asi le eŋu hena agbledede ne tsidzadza dzi ɖe kpɔtɔ. Asixɔxɔ nɔ aʋawɔʋu siawo ŋu vevietɔ le teƒe siwo tɔsisi siwo nɔa anyi ɖaa ƒe mɔnu si dzi woate ŋu aka ɖo le o. Tsi siwo wodzra ɖo la doa alɔ bligbledede kple agblemenuku bubuwo, evɔ tsigoewo kple anyigba siwo ƒo xlãe ya nye kɔƒea ƒe agbledeƒe ƒe akpa aɖe. Le nuto aɖewo me la, woɖo tsidzadzawo ɖe ɖoɖo siwo do ƒome kple wo nɔewo nu: tsi si ƒona tso tsidzɔƒe si le etame ate ŋu aʋu ayi tsidzɔƒe si le anyime, si akpe ɖe nutoawo ŋu be woawɔ tsidzadza si dzana le ɣeyiɣi aɖewo me ŋudɔ le nuto si keke ta wu me. Menye tsidzraɖoƒe koe eri la nye o. Enye kɔƒe ƒe ɖoɖo si keke ta wu si bia be woaɖe tsikpewo ɖa edziedzi, adzrae ɖo ahakpɔ edzi le ƒuƒoƒo me la ƒe akpa aɖe. Ne wodzra tsigoewo ɖo nyuie la, wokpena ɖe ame ŋu be tsi si buna to tsi si sina toa sisi si dzi womeɖu o me dzi ɖena kpɔtɔna eye wònana tsi ƒe anyinɔnɔ nyona ɖe edzi le kuɖiɣiwo.

The Grand Anicut at work: water rushing: Grand Anicut si le dɔ wɔm: tsi si le du dzi to eƒe yadoƒewo, to eƒe tsi si sina toa eme dzi eye wòyia edzi yina ɖe tɔʋu siwo le tɔʋua me. Video siwo woɖe tso Kallanai ŋuti nuŋlɔɖi si Central Institute of Classical Tamil wɔ me.
The great courtyard seen through the pal: Xɔxɔnu gã si wokpɔna to fiasãa ƒe sɔti gãwo kple aɖakaʋuwo me.
The heroine of Silappathikaram, who prov: Silappathikaram ƒe kalẽtɔ, amesi ɖo kpe srɔ̃a Kovalan ƒe fɔmaɖimaɖi dzi le Pandya-fia ŋkume to eƒe afɔkpodzi ʋuʋu me: etɔ lé kpe xɔasi siwo nye rubies, fianyɔnua ƒe dzonuwo. Agbalẽŋlɔla tsɔ wu be wòanye ŋutinya me ame si woŋlɔ ɖi, eva zu dzɔdzɔenyenye ƒe dzesi — eye wosubɔnɛ abe Pattini kple Kannaki Amman ene le Tamil Nadu, Kerala kple Sri Lanka.
The image of Shiva as Nataraja, Lord of: Shiva ƒe nɔnɔmetata si nye Nataraja, Ɣeɖuɖu ƒe Aƒetɔ, si le ɣe ɖum le dzobibi ƒe asigɛ me lae nye Cholatɔwo ƒe akɔbli ƒomevi si woɖua azã wu. Eɖea xexeame katã ƒe tsatsam si nye nuwɔwɔ, wo takpɔkpɔ, kple wo gbagbã fiana.
The Jambai inscription in Villupuram dis: Jambai nuŋɔŋlɔ si le Villupuram nutoa me yɔ ŋkɔ be “Satiyaputo Atiyan Netuman Anci”, si do ƒome kple Atiyamantɔwo ƒe amegãwo kple Satiyaputa siwo woyɔ le Ashoka ƒe sededewo me.
The Kadai Ezhu Vallalgal — Seven Great P: Kadai Ezhu Vallalgal — Amegã Adre siwo kpɔa wo ta
The Kailasanatha Temple, a Pallava-perio: Kailasanatha Gbedoxɔ, si nye Pallavatɔwo ƒe ɣeyiɣia me kpe gbedoxɔ, si me gbedoxɔ sue siwo le fli me le eƒe xɔ me.
The kalayam, the everyday Tamil clay pot: Kalaya, si nye Tamiltɔwo ƒe anyize si wozãna gbesiagbe. Eƒe ŋutilã goglo kple kɔ gbadzaa nana tsiwo fa miamiamia eye wo tsɔtsɔ bɔbɔe, eye wogatsɔa kalayamwo ƒua gbe ɖe zemela ƒe tasiaɖamfɔ dzi hedoa dzoe le kɔƒea me dzodoƒewo — si nye kadodo gbagbe aɖe kple nugo siwo woɖe le Tamiltɔwo ƒe teƒewo.
The Kallanai, or Grand Anicut, across th: Wotu Kallanai, alo Grand Anicut, si le Kaveri-tɔsisia ƒe go kemɛ dzi — si wogblɔna tso blema ke be Chola-fia Karikala ye wɔe — be woatsɔ awɔ ɖoɖo ɖe tɔsisia ƒe tsiwo ŋu ahatrɔ wo ɖe tɔdzisasrãwo me hena tsidede agble. Ena Kaveri-tɔʋua va zu Tamil Nadu ƒe bli-gbledenyigba gãwo dometɔ ɖeka, eye wògakpɔtɔ subɔa eƒe tsidede agble ƒe ɖoɖoa egbea. (Kpɔ Tsidede xɔa me hena nyatakaka bubuwo tso Tamiltɔwo ƒe tsiŋutinunya ŋu.)
The Kanchipuram silk saree is one of the: Kanchipuram seda saree nye Tamil Nadu ƒe dekɔnu avɔ siwo woɖua azã na wu la dometɔ ɖeka. Kanchipuram, si nye ŋutinya me avɔlɔlɔ̃ƒe aɖee saree sia dzɔ tso, eye wòxɔ ŋkɔ le eƒe avɔ si wotsɔ seda wɔe, zari-dɔ si me kɔ, liƒo siwo to vovo, kple nɔnɔme siwo wowɔ wònya kpɔ ta. Nutata siwo wowɔna tso blema ke dometɔ aɖewoe nye gbedoxɔxɔ kɔkɔwo, akpakpawo, mangowo, seƒoƒowo, kple nɔnɔmetata siwo wotsɔ geometri wɔe. Wozãa seda ka tsɔ lãa saree la, eye wotsɔa zari ka siwo ƒe amadede nye sika alo klosalo kpena ɖe atsyɔ̃ɖoɖo ƒe kesinɔnuwo ŋu. Kanchipuram seda sareewo xɔ nɔƒe vevi aɖe le Tamiltɔwo ƒe srɔ̃ɖeɖewo, mawusubɔsubɔkɔnuwo, azãɖuɖuwo, kple wɔna tɔxɛ bubuwo me. Avɔlɔlɔ̃ ƒe ɖoɖoa bia aɖaŋu geɖe, vevietɔ ne wozã aɖaŋu siwo wozãna tsã tsɔ blaa ŋutilã, liƒo, kple pallu. Aɖaŋudɔ sia va do le dzidzime geɖe me, eye womeɖo ƒe si tututu woɖoe anyi le ŋutinya me o. Kancheepuram Silk xɔ Geographical Indication (GI) ƒe bubu le ƒe 2005. Egbea la, saree la tsi tre ɖi na Tamil Nadu ƒe avɔlɔ̃ƒe ƒe domenyinu, aɖaŋudɔ bibi, kple dekɔnu avɔlɔlɔ̃hawo ƒe agbenɔnɔ si yi edzi.
The Kandangi saree is a traditional cott: Kandangi saree nye avɔ si wotsɔ kotoklobo wɔe si do ƒome kple Chettinad nutoa, vevietɔ Karaikudi kple nuto siwo te ɖe eŋu. Wonyae ɖe eƒe ɖaseɖiɖi siwo me kɔ, fli siwo le eŋu, liƒo siwo to vovo, kple amadede sesẽ siwo dometɔ aɖewoe nye dzĩ, sinapi, aŋutiɖiɖi, kple anyigba ƒe amadede dzẽ ta. Tso blema ke la, eƒe kotoku sesẽ la sɔ na zazã edziedzi, si ɖea gbesiagbewuwo ƒe nudidi ŋutɔŋutɔwo fiana. Kandangi avɔlɔlɔ̃ tsi tre ɖi na atsyɔ̃ɖoɖo kple avɔlɔ̃ ŋuti sidzedze tɔxɛ si le Chettinad nutoa me. Eƒe nɔnɔmewo kple amadede siwo wotsɔ tsakae na wòto vovo tso South Indiatɔwo ƒe saree kɔnyinyi bubu geɖe gbɔ. Dɔwɔwɔ ƒe ɖoɖoa bia be woadzra ka ɖo, aɖo ka siwo le avɔlɔ̃ƒea, alɔ̃ avɔa, eye woawu liƒoawo nu ahawu wo nu. Dziɖuɖua ƒe asinudɔwɔwɔwo ɖɔ kɔnyinyia be enɔ anyi ƒe 150 kple edzivɔe nye sia, togbɔ be kakaɖedzi mele ƒe si tututu wòdze egɔme tsoe ŋu o hã. Kandangi sarees xɔ GI ƒe bubu le ƒe 2019 me, kpe asi ɖe dzesidede woƒe nutome dzeside kple dekɔnu aɖaŋudɔwɔwɔ ŋu eye wòlé wo ta.
The Kaveri in flood at the anicut: Kaveritɔwo le tsiɖɔɖɔ me le anicut
The Kaveri in spate below the Grand Anic: Kaveritɔwo le ƒutsotsoewo me le Grand Anicut te. Tamil hakpanyaŋlɔlawo kafu Chola-dukɔa be enye Kaveritɔwo ƒe anyigba, amesiwo ƒe nunana medo kpo nu gbeɖe o; Silappatikaram ɖua azã nɛ be enye bli si seɖoƒe meli na o ƒe anyigba. Anicut la trɔ nunana ma wòzu ɖoɖo si dzi wokpɔna, eye tɔʋua va zu Tamil-dukɔa ƒe bligo.
The Kaveri rushing through the vents: Kaveritɔwo le du dzi to yadoƒeawo me
The Koorainadu saree is associated with: Koorainadu saree la do ƒome kple Koorainadu si te ɖe Mayiladuthurai ŋu le Tamil Nadu. Edo ƒome kple srɔ̃ɖewu siwo wodona le kɔnu nu kple avɔwo ƒe vevienyenye le dekɔnuwo me le Tamiltɔwo ƒe srɔ̃ɖeɖekɔnuwo me koŋ. Avɔ ƒomevi siwo wozãna tsã dometɔ aɖewoe nye seda kple seda-kotoku, siwo ƒe nɔnɔme kple nuwo to vovo le atsyã kple taɖodzinu tɔxɛa nu. Saree la ɖea akpa si awu siwo wolɔ̃ wɔna le ƒomea ƒe kɔnu veviwo me kple avɔlɔlɔ̃ ƒe kɔnyinyiwo ƒe kaka ɖe dzidzimewo dome fiana. Eƒe dzedzeme, avɔ, kple atsyɔ̃ɖoɖo ƒe nɔnɔmewo ate ŋu ato vovo, eyata ele be woaŋlɔ kpɔɖeŋu ɖekaɖekawo ɖe woƒe xɔtutu ŋutɔŋutɔ nu tsɔ wu be woasusui be Koorainadu saree ɖesiaɖe zɔna ɖe atsyã ɖeka dzi. Womeɖo kpe ƒe si tututu me kɔnyinyi sia dzɔ tso dzi sesĩe o. Koorainadu sarees gakpɔtɔ nye nyati vevi aɖe hena ƒomedodo si le awudodo, nutome ƒe dzedzeme, aɖaŋudɔwɔwɔ, kple kɔnuwɔwɔ ƒe agbenɔnɔ dome le Tamil Nadu la me dzodzro.
The Kovai Kora cotton saree is associate: Kovai Kora kotoku saree la do ƒome kple Coimbatore kple nuto si ƒo xlãe si me wowɔa avɔ le. Wotsɔa kotoklobo wɔe, eye wokpɔa ŋudzedze ɖe eƒe atsyɔ̃ɖoɖo si meɖi naneke o, eƒe nɔnɔme si fa, kple eƒe liƒo siwo wowɔna le blema ta. Ne wotsɔ Kora ƒe kotoklobo ƒe avɔwo sɔ kple seda saree siwo woɖo atsyɔ̃ na vevie la, zi geɖe la, wotea gbe ɖe kotoku ƒe dzedzeme le dzɔdzɔme nu, alesi woate ŋu adoe nyuie, kple alesi wowɔe tsitotsito si menya kpɔna dzea sii bɔbɔe o dzi. Saree la ɖea kotoku ƒe agbledede, ka wɔwɔ, avɔlɔlɔ̃, kple avɔlɔ̃ƒe ƒe vevienyenye fiana le Tamil Nadu. Asitɔtrɔ ƒe saree wɔwɔ bia be woadzra ka siwo wotsɔ lãgbalẽ wɔe kple esiwo wotsɔ lãfu wɔe ɖo nyuie eye woawɔ avɔlɔ̃mɔ̃a ŋudɔ aɖaŋutɔe. Kora kotoku sɔ na wɔna vovovowo, siwo dometɔ aɖewoe nye gbesiagbewudodo kple kpekpe siwo wowɔna le ɖoɖo nu. Kovai Kora Cotton xɔ GI ƒe bubu le ƒe 2008. Womeɖo ƒe si tututu wòɖoe anyi o, gake kɔnyinyia gakpɔtɔ nye dukɔa ƒe kotoku-lãgbalẽ ƒe domenyinu vovovoawo ƒe kpɔɖeŋu vevi aɖe.
The larger digitisation catalogued under: Digitization gãtɔ si woŋlɔ ɖe xexlẽdzesi ma ke te, 603 D: aŋgba ƒe nɔnɔmetata siwo wu alafa ade le babla si me wodzra Kar Narpathu ɖo la me.
The last leaf of the bundle: Agba mamlɛtɔ si le babla la me
The Leiden plates record a Chola grant o: Leiden ƒe agbalẽawo ŋlɔ Cholatɔwo ƒe kɔƒe aɖe ƒe kpekpeɖeŋunana Buddhatɔwo ƒe vihara aɖe le Nagapattinam, si Rajaraja I de se eye woɖee ɖe go le Rajendra I ƒe kpɔkplɔ te. Fifia wodzra wo ɖo ɖe Leiden, le Netherlands.
The literary image of ancient Tamil mari: Blema Tamiltɔwo ƒe ƒudzinudzedziname ƒe nɔnɔmetata si woŋlɔ ɖe agbalẽ me.
The long pillared cloister that encloses: Saɖagaxɔ didi si ŋu sɔtiwo le si ƒo xlã Brihadisvara gbedoxɔa ƒe xɔxɔnu, si me lingamwo le fli me le eƒe anyigba. Wota eƒe gliwo le Nayak ƒe ɣeyiɣia me kple nukpɔkpɔ viviwo — afisiae Shiva ƒe gana siwo ƒe ƒodo le ze me, eƒe subɔvi sue siwo le fefem — le Tamilgbe me nuŋɔŋlɔwo ƒe ha aɖe te. Le nutata mawo siwo wota emegbe megbe la, le mɔ si ƒo xlã kɔkɔeƒea la, gbedoxɔa ƒe Cholatɔwo ƒe nɔnɔmetata gbãtɔwo le.
The longest of the Ten Idylls, by Mangud: Idyll Ewoawo dometɔ diditɔ kekeake, si Mangudi Maruthanar ŋlɔ, si woŋlɔ na Pandya-fia Nedunchezhiyan. Eƒo nu tso du gã si nye Madurai ŋu tso ŋdi va se ɖe zã eye wòɖo ŋku edzi na fia la tufafatɔe be xexeame ƒe ŋutikɔkɔe katã nu yina.
The lotus pool of Sittanavasal, the Pall: Sittanavasal ƒe lotus-ta, Pallava mawunɔ si le Panamalai, Cholatɔwo ƒe glitatawo kple Nayaktɔwo ƒe glitata siwo le Gbedoxɔ Gã si le Thanjavur, kple Tanjoretɔwo ƒe nutata siwo wotsɔ sika wɔe.
The Madurai Sungudi saree is a tradition: Madurai Sungudi saree nye avɔ si wotsɔ kotoklobo wɔe si do ƒome kple Madurai, si nye ŋutinya me dekɔnuwo kple asitsaƒe aɖe le Tamil Nadu. Eƒe nɔnɔme siwo me fliwo le, eƒe nɔnɔme siwo le amadede vovovowo me, kple aɖaŋu siwo wozãna tsã tsɔ blaa nu alo tsɔa amadede tsia tre ɖe eŋu tae wòto vovo. Woblaa avɔa ƒe akpa suewo alo kpɔa wo ta le amadede dem me be woawɔ nɔnɔme tɔxɛwo ne woʋu nusi wotsɔ wɔe. Wodea asixɔxɔ Sungudi avɔwo ŋu le woƒe dzedzeme si dzea ame ŋu, avɔ si wotsɔ kotoklobo wɔe si mebɔbɔ o, kple alesi wosɔ na gbesiagbe kple azãɖuɖu ƒe awuwo ta. Aɖaŋudɔa ƒoa avɔ dzadzraɖo, bablamɔnu, amadede dede, kple eƒe nuwuwu ŋuti sidzedze nu ƒu. Eƒe ŋutinya me dzɔtsoƒe meku ɖe ƒe ɖeka si woŋlɔ ɖi dedie si dzi wòdze egɔme tsoe ŋu o. Madurai Sungudi xɔ GI ƒe bubu le ƒe 2005 me, eye wòlɔ̃ ɖe eƒe hadede kple nutoa dzi. Kɔnyinyia ɖe alesi Tamil aɖaŋudɔwɔlawo to amadede ƒe aɖaŋu tɔxɛwo kple avɔwɔwɔ ƒe mɔnu siwo woɖo anyi le nutoa me to avɔlɔlɔ̃ ƒe nɔnɔme tɔxɛwo vɛ la fia.
The masonry arches that now crown the an: Aɖakaʋu siwo wotsɔ kpe tu siwo ɖo blema tɔdzisasrãa ƒe fiakuku fifia. Britaintɔ mɔ̃ɖaŋudɔwɔla siwo srɔ̃ nu tso Kallanai ŋu le ƒe alafa wuiadelia me la wɔ dɔ ɖe edzi ŋutɔ: Aƒetɔ Arthur Cotton srɔ̃ nu tso eƒe gɔmeɖoanyiwo me hafi tu Upper Anicut to Kollidam-tɔsisia ƒe go kemɛ dzi le ƒe 1836 me, eye Richard Baird Smith kafui le ƒe 1850-awo me be enye dɔ wɔnuku aɖe si nɔ anyi ƒe alafa geɖe. Woawoe tsɔ ŋkɔ nɛ be “Grand Anicut”.
The Meenakshi Amman Temple, historic str: Meenakshi Amman Gbedoxɔa, ŋutinya me ablɔwo, mawusubɔsubɔ ƒe kɔnyinyiwo, kple agbalẽŋɔŋlɔ kple dekɔnu ƒe nuwɔna siwo yi edzi do ƒome kple egbegbe Madurai kple eƒe ŋutinya didi aɖe.
The memorial hall to Karikal Chozhan at: Karikal Chozhan ƒe ŋkuɖodzixɔ si le Kallanai, si Tamil Nadu Dziɖuɖua fɔ ɖe dzi. Woɖoa ŋku Karikalan, si nye Pattinappalai kple Porunarruppadai ƒe kalẽtɔ dzi le Tamiltɔwo ƒe kɔnyinyiwo me be enye fia si ɖu Kaveritɔwo dzi. Emegbe Cholatɔwo ƒe hakpanyawo abe Kulothunga Cholan Ula ene, kple fiaƒome siwo gblɔ be yewotsoe ƒe nuŋɔŋlɔwo gblɔ be eyae do Kaveri ƒe ƒutawo ɖe dzi.
The mini-map in the corner shows the who: Anyigbatata sue si le dzogoea dzi la ɖe blemanudzraɖoƒe bliboa fia; aŋutrɔ dzĩ lae nye wò, si fia mɔ si dzi nèdze ŋgɔe. Ʋu anyigbatata bliboa (alo Anyigbatata ƒe dzesi) eye nàtia akpata alo xɔ ɖesiaɖe si nàzɔ ayi afima.
The monuments of Mamallapuram, carved ma: Mamallapuram ƒe ŋkuɖodzinu siwo wokpa koŋ le ƒe alafa 7 lia kple 8 lia M.Ŋ. Ƒuƒoƒoa nye UNESCO ƒe Xexeame ƒe Domenyinu.
The monuments themselves, with Pallava i: Ŋkuɖodzikpeawo ŋutɔ, siwo dzi woŋlɔ Pallavatɔwo ƒe nuŋɔŋlɔwo kple fia ƒe dzesideŋkɔwo ɖo.
The most celebrated of the Seven Great P: Amesi Woɖua azã na wu le Ametakpɔla Gã Adreawo dome. Tamiltɔwo ƒe kɔnyinyi ɖo ŋku edzi be etsɔ eya ŋutɔ ƒe tasiaɖam na jasmine (mullai) creeper si si naneke meli wòali o — dɔmenyonyo si keke ta wu amewo va ɖo dzɔdzɔmexexea gbɔ. Wokpɔ eƒe xɔlɔ̃wɔwɔ kple hakpanyaŋlɔla Kapilar, eƒe Parambu Nadu taʋiʋli tso fia etɔ̃ siwo woɖo fiakuku dzi, kple vianyɔnu Angavai kple Sangavai ƒe konyifafa (Purananuru 112) ta le Sangam hakpanyawo me; tasiaɖam ŋutinya la nyo wu be woaxlẽe be enye agbalẽŋɔŋlɔ ƒe kɔnyinyi.
The mountains and the land around them,: Towo kple anyigba si ƒo xlã wo, le zãtitina le fafaɣi. Eƒe mawue nye Murugan (Seyon), eye eƒe seƒoƒoe nye kurinji, si sea seƒoƒo zi ɖeka le ƒe wuieve me. Eƒe tanyae nye punarthal, si nye lɔlɔ̃tɔwo ƒe kpekpe le adzame. Emetɔwo ƒoa anyitsi nu ƒu, dzɔa millet-gblewo ŋu tso akpɔkplɔwo gbɔ eye wodea adelã le ave me.
The murasu is the great drum of Sangam l: Murasu nye Sangam agbalẽwo ƒe kpẽ gã, si woƒona na fiawo, na aʋawɔwɔ, na dutoƒo gbeƒãɖeɖewo kple kɔnuwɔwɔwo — eƒe gbe ŋutɔ nye fia ƒe ŋusẽ ƒe dzesi. Anɔ eme be kpẽ siwo woyɔna be murasu ƒe lolome, nusiwo wotsɔ wɔe kple alesi wotsɔe ƒoe to vovo le ɣeyiɣi aɖe megbe, eyata egbegbe kpẽ aɖeke menye eƒe kpɔɖeŋu tututu o; gbugbɔgatu nye nuŋlɔɖiawo gɔmeɖeɖe.
The museum’s historical research guide t: Blemanudzraɖoƒea ƒe ŋutinya me numekuku mɔfiame si ku ɖe avɔlɔlɔ̃ ŋu le Tamil Nadu tso blema vaseɖe fifia: ɣeyiɣi ƒe ɖoɖo, nuwo kple alesi wowɔa dɔe, Sangam ƒe nuŋlɔɖiwo kple blematomenukulawo ƒe kpeɖodziwo, titinaɣeyiɣiwo, dutanyigbadzinɔɣiwo kple egbegbe ɣeyiɣiwo, kple eƒe dzɔtsoƒewo, le Eŋlisigbe me.
The museum’s notes on eight historic pla: Blemanudzraɖoƒea ƒe nuŋlɔɖi siwo ku ɖe Tamil Nadu ƒe ŋutinya me teƒe enyi ŋu, ɣemaɣi kple fifia, le Eŋlisigbe me.
The museum’s notes on eight saree tradit: Blemanudzraɖoƒea ƒe nuŋlɔɖi siwo ku ɖe Tamil Nadu ƒe saree kɔnyinyi enyi ŋu — afisi wolɔ̃ wo dometɔ ɖesiaɖe le, alesi wolɔ̃e, kple ɣeyiɣi si wòxɔ Anyigba ƒe Dzesi ƒe dzeside — le Eŋlisigbe me.
The museum’s notes on fifteen foods and: Blemanudzraɖoƒea ƒe nuŋlɔɖi siwo ku ɖe nuɖuɖu kple nusiwo wotsɔ wɔa nuɖuɖu wuiatɔ̃ siwo le Tamiltɔwo ƒe nuɖaɖa ŋutinya me ŋu, tso bli kple lãgbalẽgolo dzi va ɖo detsiƒonuwo kple nuɖuɖu siwo woɖuna le akɔɖu aŋgba dzi, kple nɔnɔmetata si dzi woŋlɔ nu ɖo, le Eŋlisigbe me.

The nadaswaram is the great double-reed: Nadaswaram nye Tamil gbedoxɔ me hadzidzi ƒe yaƒoƒo ƒe haƒonu gã si wotsɔ aŋɔ eve wɔe, si ɖina le azãɖuƒewo, srɔ̃ɖeƒewo kple amewo ƒe mɔzɔzɔwo me. Ati legbe aɖe si me asibidɛwo ƒe dowo le la wu enu ɖe ​​gaƒoɖokui si le dzo dam me; aŋɔ kple bore naa eƒe gbeɖiɖi sẽŋu si tsɔa nu. Ebia gbɔgbɔ dzi ɖuɖu kple gbeɖiɖi nyui, eƒoa ɣeyiɣi didi classical improvisations, ragas kple hakpakpawo — zi geɖe le hadome kple thavil.
The name seems to have been borne by mor: Edze abe nyɔnu hakpanyaŋlɔla siwo wu ɖeka ye tsɔ ŋkɔa ene. Sangam Avvaiyar ƒe hakpanya siwo le Purananuru, Akananuru, Kurunthogai kple Natrinai me ƒo nu tso fiawo, dɔmenyonyo kple ku ŋu; enye Adhiyaman ƒe aɖaŋuɖola si dzi woka ɖo. Ðeviwo ƒe agbalẽ xɔŋkɔ siwo nye Aathichudi, Kondrai Vendhan kple Nalvazhi nye Avvaiyar aɖe si va emegbe tɔ.
The Noyyal River region of Tamil Nadu pr: Noyyal Tɔsisi ƒe nuto si le Tamil Nadu nye tsizazã ƒe kpɔɖeŋu bubu to tsidzɔƒewo kple tɔdzisasrã siwo do ƒome kplii ƒe kadodo aɖe dzi. Le esi teƒe be nutoawo nanɔ te ɖe tɔsisi ƒe sisi tẽ dzi ko la, woto nudzraɖoƒe siwo kpena ɖe ame ŋu be woalé tsi siwo li ahama wo. Tɔdziʋu siwo le kadodo mawo me ate ŋu aƒo tsidzadza kple tsi si sina le ɣeyiɣi aɖe me nu ƒu, eye woadzra wo ɖo be woazãe emegbe le agbledede me. Woƒe viɖe nɔ te ɖe ɖoɖo si nu anyigbaa le, alesi tɔdzisasrãwo le, tɔdzisasrãwo ƒe ŋutete kple ɣeyiɣi si me tsi dza dzi. Ne wolé be nɛ nyuie la, kadodo si le kadodo me kpena ɖe ame ŋu wòkaka tsi siwo seɖoƒe li na le teƒe geɖe. Woda asi ɖe Noyyal Tɔsisi ƒe ɖoɖoa hã dzi le India ƒe tsi ƒe domenyinu ŋuti nuŋlɔɖiwo me. Eɖe nusita wòle be woase tsidede agble tso blema ke gɔme be enye xɔtunu siwo do ƒome kplii ƒe kadodo tsɔ wu be woanye tsidzɔƒe siwo sa ɖe aga ƒe ƒuƒoƒo.

The pambai is a pair of drums played tog: Pambai nye kpẽ eve siwo woƒo ɖekae, woƒe gbe bɔbɔe kple kɔkɔ siwo to vovo la ʋãa amewo ƒe fefewo, amewo ƒe zɔzɔ kple kɔƒe me azãɖuɖuwo le Tamil Nadu godoo. Ewɔa dɔ ɣeyiɣi didi aɖee nye sia na gbeƒãɖeɖewo, kɔnuwɔwɔwo, azãɖuɖuwo kple kunuwɔwɔwo, eye egbe ƒe parai attam kpena ɖe kpẽkuku ŋu tsɔ ɖua ɣe. The ripe paddy is cut by hand with sickl: Wotsɔa asi lãa bli si tsi la, eye wotsɔa hɛwo lãnɛ, emegbe woƒonɛ be woama nukua ɖe vovo tso aŋgbaawo gbɔ eye wotsɔa ya ƒoa woe be woaɖe gbeawo ɖa. The Salem silk saree is associated with: Wotsɔ Salem seda saree la do ƒome kple Salem, si nye nuto vevi aɖe si me wowɔa avɔ le le Tamil Nadu. Wotsɔa seda ka lɔ̃a saree siawo, eye woƒe amadede le vovovo, woƒe liƒo ƒe nɔnɔmewo, kple atsyɔ̃ɖoɖo ƒe nɔnɔme vovovowo le wo ŋu. Woƒe dzedzeme ate ŋu atso atsyã bɔbɔe siwo wowɔ wònya kpɔ dzi va ɖo avɔ siwo wowɔ wònya kpɔ wu siwo woɖo na srɔ̃ɖeƒewo, azãɖuɖuwo, kple wɔna tɔxɛ bubuwo dzi. Salem ƒe avɔlɔ̃ƒe ƒe domenyinu do ƒome kple seda wɔwɔ, avɔlɔlɔ̃, kple avɔlɔ̃ƒe ƒe asiwo ƒe ŋgɔyiyi si keke ta wu le Tamil Nadu. Aɖaŋudɔa bia aɖaŋudɔwɔwɔ le ka dzadzraɖo, avɔlɔ̃mɔ̃a ɖoɖo, avɔlɔ̃ ƒe tete si nɔa anyi ɖaa, kple avɔa wuwu me. Salem Silk xɔ GI ƒe bubu le ƒe 2007 me, eye wòlɔ̃ ɖe eƒe nutome dzedzeme dzi le se nu. Ɣletiŋkeke sia si dzi woŋlɔ ŋkɔ ɖo la mefia ɣeyiɣi si me kɔnyinyia dze egɔme o. Egbea la, Salem seda gakpɔtɔ nye Tamil Nadu ƒe avɔlɔ̃ƒe vovovowo ƒe domenyinu ƒe akpa aɖe eye wòɖe nutome avɔlɔlɔ̃ dɔwɔƒewo ƒe vevienyenye fia le dekɔnu ƒe aɖaŋuwo takpɔkpɔ kple asinudɔwɔwɔwo ƒe agbenɔnɔ ŋuti kpekpeɖeŋu nana me.
