The sea routes that joined the Tamil coa: Ƒudzimɔ siwo ƒo ƒu ɖe Tamil ƒuta yi Ƒudzĩa gbɔ, Mediterranea kple Anyieheɣedzeƒe Asia, melidzeƒeawo ƒe xɔtuɖaŋu — melidzeƒewo, vudowo kple anyikpe melidzeƒewo — kple nugoewo, zewo kple adzɔnu siwo zɔa mɔ le wo dome — kple Adichanallur, si nye Gaɣeyiɣia me yɔdo si le Thamirabarani balia me, le nɔnɔmetata siwo meʋãna o kple sinima me.
The secret of Kallanai’s endurance: clay: Kallanai ƒe dzidodo ƒe nya ɣaɣla: anyi kple tsiɖɔɖɔ nyui siwo tsiɖɔɖɔ tsɔna la wɔa dɔ yia teƒe siwo le kpeawo dome eye wotrea wo nu. Tɔsisia kpe asi ɖe eya ŋutɔ ƒe tɔdzisasrã tutu ŋu, eye tsiɖɔɖɔ ɖesiaɖe si gblẽ ɖi yeye ɖi la na nutrenua gawɔ yeye. Le kɔnyinyi nu la, mɔxenu sia si wotsɔ kpe kple anyi wɔ la le tɔsisi gbagbe aɖe me ƒe akpe eve kloe enye sia.
The shore at Poompuhar in Mayiladuthurai: Ƒuta si le Poompuhar le Mayiladuthurai nutoa me, afisi ƒuta ƒe tɔtrɔ kple tsidzadza trɔ asi le blema melidzeƒea ƒe nɔnɔme ŋu le.
The shore at Poompuhar today, near the m: Ƒuta si le Poompuhar egbea, si te ɖe Kaveri-tɔsisia ƒe nugbɔ ŋu, afisi Cholatɔwo ƒe melidzeƒe gbãtɔ si nye Puhar nɔ tsã. Numekuku siwo wowɔ le tsi te ɖe kpewo fia le ƒuta sia; wogale nu srɔ̃m tso afisi blemadu la ɖo, kple alesi ƒuta trɔe ŋu.
The Shore Temple and its grounds beside: Shore Gbedoxɔa kple eƒe anyigba si le atsiaƒu to, si wokpɔ tso dziƒo.
The Shore Temple in an early painting: Shore Gbedoxɔa le nutata gbãtɔ aɖe me
The Shore Temple on the Coromandel Coast: Shore Gbedoxɔ si le Coromandel Ƒuta, si nye Ŋkuɖodzinuwo ƒe Ƒuƒoƒo si le Mahabalipuram, si nye UNESCO ƒe Xexeame ƒe Domenyinu Teƒe, ƒe akpa aɖe.
The shortest of the Ten Idylls, by Nappu: Idyll Ewoawo dometɔ kpuitɔ kekeake, si Napputhanar ŋlɔ. Woɖee fia le ave (mullai) ƒe nɔnɔme me le tsidzaɣi, eye wòɖe srɔ̃nyɔnu aɖe si le lalam dzigbɔɖitɔe be ye srɔ̃ natrɔ tso aʋa me la fia.
The signature pottery of the Tamil Iron: Tamiltɔwo ƒe Gaɣeyiɣia me ze siwo wotsɔ asi ŋlɔe nye nusiwo wotsɔ yibɔ kple dzĩ wɔe: dzĩ le gota, yibɔ si le keklẽm le eme kple eƒe gowo. Zemelawo te ŋu ɖoa esia gbɔ to tudada ɖe nugoawo me, ale be akpa si wokpɔ ta na tso yame la trɔ zu yibɔ. Ze mawo tɔgbe geɖe tsɔa dzesiwo alo nuŋɔŋlɔ siwo woŋlɔ ɖe anyi me, eye tso ŋutinya me ɣeyiɣia ƒe gɔmedzedze la, ŋkɔ siwo woŋlɔ ɖe Tamil-Brahmi — Tamilgbe me nuŋɔŋlɔ xoxotɔ kekeake — me le Keeladi, Kodumanal, Arikamedu kple didiƒe ʋĩ abe Sri Lanka, Thailand kple Egipte ƒe Ƒudzĩa ƒe ƒuta.
The surviving halls, pillars, arches and: Akpatawo, sɔtiwo, aɖakaʋuwo kple xɔxɔnu siwo gakpɔtɔ li la kpɔa Nayaktɔwo ƒe xɔtuɖaŋu ƒe kpɔɖeŋu veviwo ta, togbɔ be xɔ gbãtɔ bliboa megali o hã.
The temple and its fort walls today: Gbedoxɔa kple eƒe gli sesẽwo egbea
The temple complex from above, within th: Gbedoxɔ gã la tso dziƒo, le egbegbe dugã si nye Thanjavur me.
The temple complex in the modern city: Gbedoxɔ gã si le egbegbe dugã me
The temple enclosure from directly above: Gbedoxɔa ƒe xɔ si wotu tso etame tẽ
The temple enclosure seen from directly: Gbedoxɔa ƒe xɔ si wotsɔ ƒo xlãe si wokpɔ tso etame tẽ: vimana, mandapa didi la, gbedoxɔ siwo ƒo xlã xɔxɔnua kple vudo si ƒe mo le goglo si ƒe mo le abe dzata ene le mɔa gbɔ.
The temple from the air, its gopurams ri: Gbedoxɔa tso yame, eƒe gopuramwo le dzi yim ɖe egbegbe du si tsi ƒo xlãe ƒe ablɔwo dzi.
The temple, sculptural details, inscript: Gbedoxɔa, kpememewo, nuŋɔŋlɔwo kple blematomenukulawo ƒe kpeɖodziwo kpɔa teƒea ƒe fiaɖuƒe kple mawusubɔsubɔ ƒe vevienyenye ƒe kpeɖodziwo ta.
The temple’s own inscriptions record its: Gbedoxɔa ŋutɔ ƒe nuŋɔŋlɔwo ŋlɔ eƒe xɔtutu, nunanawo kple atikplɔwo tsitotsito.
The Ten Idylls and the Eight Anthologies: The Ten Idylls and the Eight Anthologies — Tamiltɔwo ƒe hakpanya gbãtɔwo, le CICT ƒe tatawo me.
The Thamirabarani — known in Tamil as th: Thamirabarani — si woyɔna le Tamilgbe me be Porunai — sina toa ameɖibɔa ŋu ne ele mɔ dzi yina Mannar-ƒuta. Korkai, si nye Pandya melidzeƒe si xɔ ŋkɔ le eƒe dzonuwo ta la nɔ tɔsisia ƒe anyime; abe alesi sinimaa de dzesii ene la, bali sia me tɔwo te ŋu ɖoa atsiaƒua gbɔ, kple mɔ siwo to edzi, to tɔsisia dzi. Tɔsisi la na agble nyuiwo, tsi kple mɔ si yi ƒuta va nɔ balia me.
The thavil, closely tied to the Thanjavu: Thavil, si bla ɖe Thanjavur nutoa ŋu kplikplikpli la nye kpẽ si le abe ʋuƒo ene eye ta le eƒe nugbɔ ɖesiaɖe, eye wotsɔ asi ɖeka ƒoe ɖe ta ɖeka dzi eye wotsɔ ati kpui aɖe ƒoe ɖe evelia dzi. Le nadaswaram haƒoha me la, ewɔa nu geɖe wu ɣeyiɣi léle ɖe asi ko: fefewɔla bibiwo tsɔa ɣeyiɣi ƒe tɔtrɔ kple ŋusẽ ɖoa hadzidzia ŋu, eye woƒe gbe sesẽ ale gbegbe be woate ŋu awɔ gota gome mɔzɔzɔwo kple gbedoxɔ me kpekpe gãwo.
The Thirubuvanam silk saree originates f: Thirubuvanam seda saree la dzɔ tso Thirubuvanam le Thanjavur nuto me le Tamil Nadu. Etsi tre ɖi na seda ƒe kɔnyinyi tɔxɛ aɖe si me aɖaŋudɔwɔlawo wɔa seda avɔ siwo le amadede vovovowo me siwo wotsɔ liƒo siwo wolɔ̃ kple dekɔnu ƒe nɔnɔmetatawo ɖo atsyɔ̃ na. Le alesi wowɔ sareewoe nu la, woate ŋu awɔ nɔnɔmetata siwo wowɔ wònya kpɔ, amadede siwo to vovo, kple atsyɔ̃ɖonu siwo sɔ na azãɖuɖu kple kɔnuwɔwɔ ƒe awuwo. Kɔnyinyia ɖe nutoa me ƒe hadede ɣeyiɣi didi aɖe kple avɔlɔlɔ̃ kple avɔlɔlɔ̃ ŋuti sidzedze ƒe kaka ɖe dzidzimewo me fia. Seda saree wɔwɔ bia be woabi ɖe ka dzadzraɖo, avɔlɔ̃ƒe ƒe dɔwɔwɔ, nɔnɔmetata wɔwɔ, kple avɔ ƒe nuwuwu me. Togbɔ be womekpɔ ƒe si tututu me wòdzɔ tso o hã la, Thirubuvanam gakpɔtɔ nye nutome ŋkɔ vevi aɖe le Tamil Nadu ƒe seda-lãgbalẽtata ƒe domenyinu me. Eƒe sareewo ɖe alesi avɔlɔlɔ̃ƒe vovovowo tu atsyã tɔxɛwo kple ŋkɔ nyuiwo ɖo esime wole kpekpem ɖe South Indiatɔwo ƒe avɔlɔ̃nuwo ƒe ŋutinya si keke ta wu ŋu la fia.
The Thirukkural by Thiruvalluvar: 1,330: Thirukkural si Thiruvalluvar ŋlɔ: fli eve ƒe nya eve 1,330 siwo le ta 133 me, siwo woma ɖe agbalẽ etɔ̃ me — Nɔnɔme Nyui (Aram), Kesinɔnuwo (Porul), kple Lɔlɔ̃ (Inbam). Woɖe egɔme ɖe xexeame ƒe gbegbɔgblɔ geɖewo me.
The Thirukkural could not be opened just: Womete ŋu ʋu Thirukkural la fifia ko o. Taflatse do agbalẽ xatsaxatsaa eye nàgadze agbagba ake.
The three crowned kings of the Tamil lan: Dzesi aɖe nɔ Tamil-nyigba dzi fia etɔ̃ siwo woɖo fiakuku na la dometɔ ɖesiaɖe ŋu, eye woƒe gakuwo tsɔ wo: Cholatɔwo ƒe amegãxi, Pandyatɔwo ƒe tɔmelã, kple Cheratɔwo ƒe dati. Ne woxlẽ dzesi siawo ɖekae la, wogblɔa dunyahehe ŋutinya — ne Cholatɔwo ƒe gaku aɖe ɖe amegãxi si ŋu Pandya tɔmelã kple Chera-ti le axadzi la fia la, eɖea gbeƒã Chola-fia ƒe aɖaŋudzedze ɖe eƒe hoʋlilawo dzi.
The Tirukkural contains 1,330 couplets a: Nya eve 1,330 ye le Tirukkural la me, eye woɖo wo ɖe ta 133 me. Womae ɖe akpa etɔ̃ me: Nɔnɔme Nyui, Kesinɔnuwo kple Lɔlɔ̃. Dɔa ƒo nu tso ame ŋutɔ ƒe agbenɔnɔ, ƒomegbenɔnɔ, xɔlɔ̃wɔwɔ, sukudede, dziɖuɖu, dzɔdzɔenyenye kple dɔmetɔtrɔ ŋu.
The Tirukkural has been translated into: Woɖe Tirukkural gɔme ɖe gbegbɔgblɔ gbogbo aɖewo me, si na Thiruvalluvar ƒe susuwo ɖo nuxlẽlawo gbɔ wu Tamiltɔwo ƒe agbalẽwo ƒe liƒowo.
The Tiruvalangadu plates of Rajendra I a: Rajendra I ƒe Tiruvalangadu-gbadzɛwo kple Sundara Chola ƒe Anbil-gbadzɛwo nye Chola-fiaƒomea ƒe dzidzimegbalẽ kple ŋutinyatsoƒe veviwo.
The Tolkappiyam by Tolkappiyar is the ol: Tolkappiyam si Tolkappiyar ŋlɔ lae nye Tamilgbe me gbeŋutise xoxotɔ kekeake si gakpɔtɔ li. Eƒe agbalẽ etɔ̃awo ƒo nu tso ŋɔŋlɔdzesiwo kple gbeɖiɖiwo (Ezhuthu), nyawo (Sol), kple agbe kple hakpanyawo (Porul) ŋu.
The udukkai is a small hourglass-shaped: Udukkai nye kpẽ sue aɖe si ƒe nɔnɔme le abe gaƒoɖokui ene, eye wotsɔ ka siwo tea eƒe ta eveawo ƒo ƒui; kaawo mimi ate ŋu atrɔ gbeɖiɖia. Wolée ɖe asi ɖeka me eye wotsɔ asi evelia ƒoe, ekplɔa mawusubɔsubɔhawo, amewo ƒe ŋutinyawo kple kɔnuwɔwɔwo ɖo — si nye ŋkuɖodzinu na alesi ƒoƒo, ɖokuitsɔtsɔna kple nuƒoƒo ƒe nuwɔna bla ɖekae kplikplikpli.
The ural and ulakkai were used to pound: Wozãa ural kple ulakkai tsɔ ƒoa bli, millet, nukuwo kple nu ʋeʋĩwo. Ural nye nugo sesẽ aɖe, eye zi geɖe la, wotsɔa ati alo kpe wɔae, evɔ ulakkai ya nyea dɔwɔnu didi aɖe si wotsɔ ƒoa nu. Wo ame evea kpe asi ɖe wo ŋu woɖea nukuwo ɖa, wogbãa nukuwo eye wodzraa nusiwo woatsɔ aɖa nu ɖo. Dɔwɔnuawo ɖea ŋutilãme agbagbadzedze kple dɔ si wowɔna ɖekae si wowɔna le nuɖuɖu siwo woɖana le blema me hã fiana.
The veenai (Saraswati veena) is one of t: Veenai (Saraswati veena) nye haƒonu vevi siwo wotsɔa ka ƒoa South Indiatɔwo ƒe haƒoƒo xoxowo dometɔ ɖeka: ati gã aɖe si wotsɔ ƒoa ha, kɔ didi si ŋu fretted, ka kple tuning pegs, zi geɖe la, gbeɖiɖi evelia nɔa eŋu. Kaawo tete kple wo tsɔtsɔ ƒu gbe ɖe fret-awo ŋu naa Carnatic hadzidziwo nyea atsyɔ̃ɖonu nyuiwo. Esi wòdo ƒome kple Saraswati, si nye nusɔsrɔ̃ ƒe mawunɔ ta la, ele be wòade vovototoe tso blema yazh gbɔ — si sɔ le akpa si wòwɔna me, gake menye eƒe dzidzimevi tẽ o.
The walls of the Brihadeeswarar temple c: Brihadeeswarar gbedoxɔa ƒe gliwo dzi woŋlɔ Rajaraja I ƒe nuŋɔŋlɔ didi siwo yɔ nunanawo, gbedoxɔa me dɔwɔlawo, kpe xɔasiwo, kple nunanawo — si nye nuŋlɔɖi ɖedzesi aɖe tso gbedoxɔa ŋu be enye dɔwɔƒe.
The Way of Maintaining the Family: Mɔ si dzi woato alé ƒomea me ɖe asi
The wooden plough, often drawn by cattle: Wozãa atikutsetse si nyiwo alo nyitsuwo hea zi geɖe tsɔ ɖea agbledenyigbawo hedzrana wo ɖo hena nukuwo ƒaƒã. Esi wònye asidɔwɔnu siwo wotsɔ doa nukuwo heɖea gbewo, lãgbalẽŋudɔwɔnuwo hena nuŋeŋe, kple ŋeŋe kple yaƒoƒo tsɔ kɔ nukuawo ŋu ta la, enye dɔwɔnu siwo agbledelawo trɔna ɖe woawo ŋutɔ ƒe anyigba kple agblemenukuwo ŋu eye wotsɔa wo tso dzidzime ɖeka me yia bubu me la tɔ.
The woodland and pastures, in the evenin: Avenyigbawo kple lãnyiƒewo, le tsidzaɣi ƒe fiẽ me. Eƒe mawue nye Mayon (Thirumal), eye eƒe seƒoƒo nye jasmine (mullai). Eƒe tanyae nye iruthal — lala dzigbɔɖi, esime kalẽtɔa le lalam be srɔ̃a natrɔ ava hafi tsi nadza. Emetɔwo nye lãnyila siwo kpɔa nyiwo dzi eye woƒoa lãgbalẽ kple bɔta.
The works that arrange their verses land: Dɔ siwo ɖoa woƒe kpukpuiwo ɖe ɖoɖo nu ɖe ​​anyigba ƒe nɔnɔme nu — Ainkurunuru, Aintinai Aimpathu kple Ezhupathu, Tinaimozhi Aimpathu, Tinaimalai Nurraimpathu kple Kainnilai — le deti-aŋgba babla siwo me wogbugbɔ wo kɔ la me.
The world-famous Chola bronzes: how they: Cholatɔwo ƒe akɔbli siwo xɔ ŋkɔ le xexeame katã: alesi wotsɔ aŋɔ si bu ƒe mɔnu, Nataraja ƒe nɔnɔmetata, kple Swamimalai ƒe asinudɔwɔwɔ gbagbe wɔ woe.
The yazh is one of the most distinctive: Yazh nye haƒonu siwo ɖe dzesi wu le blema Tamiltɔwo ƒe agbalẽwo me la dometɔ ɖeka: haƒonu si wotsɔ ka ƒoe, si ƒe kekeme le abe saŋku si wotsɔ aɖaka wɔe ene. Sangam ƒe agbalẽwo abe Perumpanatrupadai, kple Silappatikaram ene, ƒo nu tso eŋu, eye wònye panar, bard siwo tsɔ hakpanyawo kpe ɖe hadzidzi ŋu la tɔ. Agbalẽnyalagãwo yɔ ƒomevi geɖe — periyazh, siriyazh, sakota yazh kple vil yazh — siwo ƒe xɔtutu tututu nuŋlɔɖiawo meɖe fia bliboe o, eyata yazh ɖesiaɖe si wokpɔ egbea nye gbugbɔgatu. Enye haƒonu le eɖokui si, ke menye veenai gbãtɔ dzro aɖe ko o.
These are food traditions associated wit: Esiawo nye nuɖuɖu ƒe kɔnyinyi siwo do ƒome kple Sangam agbalẽwo ƒe anyigba ƒe nɔnɔme kple nutoawo, ke menye nuɖuɖu siwo woɖo ɖi siwo dzi ame sia ame zɔna ɖo o. Nusiwo amewo ɖuna la to vovo le ɣeyiɣi, nutoa me, ɣeyiɣi kple asitsatsa nu. Fotoawo nye egbegbe nuɖuɖu siwo ŋu nuŋlɔɖiawo ƒo nu tsoe ƒe nɔnɔmetatawo gbugbɔgatu, ke menye blema nuɖuɖuwo o.

Thirugnanasambandar, the 7th-century chi: Thirugnanasambandar, ƒe alafa 7 lia me ɖevi kɔkɔe, Shaiva Nayanmar gã siwo ƒe hadzidziwo ʋu Tevaram la dometɔ ɖeka. Chola akɔbliwo ɖee fia abe ŋutsuvi sue aɖe si le ɣe ɖum le dzidzɔkpɔkpɔ me, eƒe asibidɛ si wotsɔ fiaa nu la kɔ ɖe dzi ɖo ta Shiva gbɔ, amesi — ŋutinyaa gblɔe — na nunya ƒe notsie tso Parvati ƒe no me.
Thirumalai Nayak Palace represents the a: Thirumalai Nayak Fiasã tsi tre ɖi na xɔtuɖaŋu ƒe atsyɔ̃ɖoɖo, fia ƒe dekɔnuwo kple dunyahehe ŋutinya si nɔ anyi le Madurai Nayak ɣeyiɣia me.
Thirumalai Nayak Palace was constructed: Wotu Thirumalai Nayak Fiasã le ƒe alafa wuiadrelia me le Madurai Nayak fiaƒomea me Fia Thirumalai Nayak ƒe dziɖuɣi. Fiasãa nye fia ƒe nɔƒe kple fiasã me agbenɔnɔ ƒe teƒe vevi aɖe. Eƒe xɔtuɖaŋuwo ƒo sɔti gãwo, akpata siwo keke, atsyɔ̃ɖonuwo kple ŋusẽkpɔɖeamedzi siwo do ƒome kple Nayaktɔwo ƒe ɣeyiɣia nu ƒu. Ŋutinya me nuŋlɔɖiwo ɖee fia be fiasã gbãtɔa lolo wu akpa siwo gakpɔtɔ li egbea.
Thirumurugatrupadai, Porunaratrupadai, S: Thirumurugatrupadai, Porunaratrupadai, Sirupanatrupadai, Perumpanatrupadai, Mullaippattu, Maduraikkanchi, Nedunalvadai, Kurinjippattu, Pattinappalai, kple Malaipadukadam. Hakpanya didi siawo dometɔ aɖewoe nye “hakpanya siwo fiaa mɔ ame” (atrupadai), siwo me hakpanyaŋlɔla ɖeka fiaa mɔ bubu yia ame aɖe si tsɔa ɖe le eme na dɔmenyotɔ aɖe gbɔ.

Thiruvalluvar is celebrated as one of th: Woɖua Thiruvalluvar ƒe azã be enye hakpanyaŋlɔla gãtɔwo dometɔ ɖeka le Tamiltɔwo ƒe agbalẽwo me. Wogblɔna tso blema ke be eyae kpa Tirukkural, si nye Tamilgbe me agbalẽ xɔŋkɔ aɖe si ku ɖe amegbetɔ ƒe agbenɔnɔ ƒe akpa vevi etɔ̃ ŋu: nɔnɔme nyui, kesinɔnuwo kple lɔlɔ̃.
Thiruvalluvar occupies an important plac: Thiruvalluvar xɔ nɔƒe vevi aɖe le Tamiltɔwo ƒe agbalẽŋɔŋlɔ kple dekɔnuwo ƒe domenyinu me. Kpememe gã si le Kanyakumari kple Valluvar Kottam le Chennai le ŋkuɖodzinu ɖedzesi siwo wotsɔ ɖe adzɔgbe nɛ la dome.
Thiruvalluvar’s 1330 couplets on virtue,: Thiruvalluvar ƒe ƒe 1330 me nya eve siwo ku ɖe nɔnɔme nyui, kesinɔnuwo kple lɔlɔ̃ ŋu, siwo wogbugbɔ ŋlɔ kple Parimelazhagar ƒe ƒe alafa wuietɔ̃lia me numeɖeɖe, si nye numeɖeɖe siwo ŋu wosrɔ̃ nu tsoe wu le blema numeɖeɖewo dome.
Thiruvalluvar’s teachings encourage peop: Thiruvalluvar ƒe nufiafiawo dea dzi ƒo na amewo be woanɔ agbe anukwaretɔe, awɔ nu ɖe ​​ame bubuwo ŋu dɔmenyotɔe eye woawɔ nu dzɔdzɔe. Menye ɣeyiɣi ɖeka alo nuto ɖeka me koe eƒe nya eve ƒokpliwo le o; nuxlẽlawo ƒe dzidzimewo yi edzi le wo srɔ̃m hekpɔ ŋudzedze ɖe wo ŋu.

Water management has played a major role: Tsizazã wɔ akpa vevi aɖe le Tamil Nadu ƒe agbledede ŋutinya me elabena tsidzadza toa vovo le ɣeyiɣiwo kple nuto vovovowo me. Agbledela siwo nɔ anyi tso blema ke zãa tɔsisiwo, vudowo, tsitawo, tɔdzisasrãwo, kple tsidede agblewo tsɔ doa alɔ agbledede. Nuɖoanyi siawo do alɔ agbledede le teƒe siwo tsidzadza ɖeɖe mesɔ gbɔ le o. Wo dzi kpɔkpɔ bia be nutoa me tɔwo nawɔ nu aduadu eye woakpɔ tsidzɔƒewo dzi le agbanɔamedzi me. Tsidede agble tso blema ke gakpɔtɔ nye nya vevi aɖe si woatsɔ ase ƒomedodo si le agbledede, mɔ̃ɖaŋudɔwo, amewo ƒe nɔƒewo, kple nutome ƒe tɔtrɔ ɖe nɔnɔmewo ŋu dome le Tamil Nadu gɔme.

Weaving is more than a craft: it connect: Avɔlɔlɔ̃ menye asinudɔwɔwɔ ko o: etsɔa gbesiagbe awudodo, agbledede, mɔ̃ɖaŋununya, asitsatsa, aɖaŋudɔwɔla bibiwo, dekɔnuwo ƒe dzesidede ame kple Tamiltɔwo ƒe nutoawo ƒe agbenɔnɔ doa ka kple wo nɔewo le ƒe alafa geɖe me. Nusiwo wotsɔ wɔee nye paruthi (kotoku), si nye ka vevi aɖe si wotsɔa ka ƒoa ka helɔ̃nɛ wòzua avɔ; pattu (seda), si wonya le Anyiehe Asiatɔwo ƒe avɔlɔ̃ƒe ƒe kɔnyinyi gbãtɔwo me, togbɔ be ka siwo wozãna la to vovo le ɣeyiɣi kple teƒe nu hã; numiemie ƒe amadedewo abe indigo ene, si ŋu woƒo nu tsoe le Tamiltɔwo ƒe avɔlɔ̃gbalẽ gbãtɔwo me; kple nool (ka), ka si wotsa alo wotrona wòzua ka si nɔa anyi ɖaa si sɔ na avɔlɔ̃mɔ̃a.

Wet-field farming · the marutham landsca: Wet-field farming · marutham ƒe anyigba ƒe nɔnɔme
What each landscape gave its people to e: Nusiwo anyigba ƒe nɔnɔme ɖesiaɖe na eƒe amewo ɖu: nyi, anyitsi kple gbemetikutsetsewo le Kurinji togbɛwo dzi, notsi, aŋɔ kple bɔta le Mullai-lãnyiƒewo, bli kple nukuwo le Marutham-gblewo dzi, tɔmelã, tɔmelã ƒuƒu kple dze le Neithal ƒuta, kple nuɖuɖu siwo wotsɔ yi Palai-mɔ ƒuƒuwo dzi.
When water could not flow naturally from: Ne tsi mete ŋu sina le dzɔdzɔme nu tso tɔsisi, tsidzɔƒe alo vudo me yi agble me o la, agbledelawo hiãa mɔnu siwo dzi woato anyie. Tamiltɔwo ƒe agbledede ƒe nuwɔna siwo wowɔna tso blema ke dometɔ aɖewoe nye mɔ̃ siwo wotsɔa asi kɔa tsi abe gazewo, kusiwo kple mɔ̃ siwo wotsɔa lever wɔa dɔe. Picottah, si woɖɔna zi geɖe be enye tsi si wotsɔna tsia tsii si da sɔ la, wɔnɛ be ame te ŋu kɔa tsi kple agbagbadzedze sue aɖe ko wu esi wòtsɔa asi. Lever-mɔ̃ si wozãna ɖaa zãa ati legbe aɖe si wotu ɖe pivot dzi, eye wotsɔa nugoe aɖe dea eƒe nugbɔ ɖeka eye wotsɔa kpekpeme si tsia tre ɖe eŋu la dea eƒe nugbɔ kemɛ. Dɔwɔla la ɖiɖia nugoe la ɖe tsia me eye wòkɔnɛ ɖe dzi be wòakɔ tsi ƒuƒlu ɖe tɔdzisasrã alo agble aɖe me. Tamiltɔwo ƒe agbalẽwo, siwo dometɔ aɖewoe nye Ahananuru, Maduraikanchi kple Silappadikaram, me nya siwo gɔme woɖe be wonye tsi kɔkɔ ƒe nuwɔnawo ƒe kpeɖodzi, eye ŋutinya me nuŋɔŋlɔwo ƒo nu tso anyigba siwo wode tsii to mɔ̃ siwo le abe picottah ene zazã me ŋu. Dɔwɔnu siawo ɖe vi ŋutɔ na anyigba suewo, abɔwo me agbledede kple agble siwo le tsia tame.
Where rain was scarce and the land drier: Le afisiwo tsi medzana le o eye anyigba ƒuna wu le la, Tamil agbledelawo dea nukuwo abe kambu kple varagu ene, tsɔ kpe ɖe nukuwo, sesame kple kotoklobo ŋu. Agblemenukuwo tiatia be woasɔ na anyigba ɖesiaɖe, tsidzadza kple tsi ƒe agbɔsɔsɔme nye sidzedze si Sangam hakpanyawo ɖe fia xoxo — eye millets gakpɔtɔ le Tamil Nadu ƒe agblemenuku veviwo dome egbea.
With Puhar, one of the two centres of ea: Le Puhar, si nye Cholatɔwo ƒe ŋusẽ gbãtɔ ƒe teƒe eve siwo nɔ Kaveritɔwo dzi la dometɔ ɖeka.
With the imperial Cholas came a confiden: Fiaɖuƒea ƒe Cholatɔwo va kpe gaku si ŋu kakaɖedzi le si wotsɔ sika, klosalo kple akɔbli wɔe. Uttama Chola ƒe gaku siwo nɔ anyi le ƒe alafa 10 lia ƒe nuwuwu la tsɔ eƒe ŋkɔ, eye tso Rajaraja I dzi la, fia ƒe dzesi la ɖe Chola-amegãxi si bɔbɔ nɔ anyi si Pandya tɔmelã eve le axadzi le ɣe ƒe keklẽŋusẽti aɖe te, eye fia la ƒe ŋkɔ le Nagari ŋɔŋlɔdzesiwo me. Esi Cholatɔwo ɖu Sri Lanka dzi vɔ la, akɔbli ƒomevi aɖe si ɖe fia si le tsitrenu fia le akpa ɖeka eye ame si bɔbɔ nɔ anyi ɖe akpa kemɛ la kaka ɖe South India kple ƒukpoa dzi. Wobu asixɔxɔwo le kalanju kple kasu — nya si na Eŋlisigbe eƒe “ga” me.
Witness to the height of Chola imperial: Ðasefo le Cholatɔwo ƒe fiaɖuƒe ƒe didi vevie ƒe kɔkɔƒe ŋu; UNESCO ƒe Chola Gbedoxɔ Gã Gbagbewo ƒe akpa aɖe.
